articles.title: Black Friday: Mac Mini mit M6 weit unter 1.000 Euro – Amazon-Deal im Chek
articles.text:
Black Friday: Mac Mini mit M6 weit unter 1.000 Euro – wie gut ist das Amazon-Angebot?
Hinweis: Wir haben in diesem Artikel Provisions-Links verwendet und sie durch "*" gekennzeichnet. Erfolgt über diese Links eine Bestellung, erhält t3n.de eine Provision.
Die sogenannte „Chipkrise“ (oder RAMageddon) sorgt nach wie vor dafür, dass Smartphones und andere Computer derzeit deutlich teurer sind, als noch vor einem Jahr. Besonders deutlich wird die Entwicklung unter anderem am Preis des Mac Mini. War die M4-Version 2024 noch für 699 Euro an den Start gegangen und schnell zum Hit bei KI-Fans geworden, kostet der Nachfolger mit M6-Prozessor bei Apple mindestens 1.049 Euro. Doch am Black Friday muss man diesen Betrag nicht bezahlen. Amazon bietet den kleinen Desktop-Rechner derzeit besonders günstig an.
Mac Mini mit M6 für 835 Euro
„-20 Prozent“ steht zur Black-Friday-Woche bei Amazon neben dem Mac Mini mit M6. Während man diesen sogenannten Streichpreisen normalerweise keine allzu hohe Bedeutung beimessen sollte, da sich die Händler auch bei jahrealten Produkten in der Regel auf die Preisempfehlung der Hersteller beziehen, stellt der Mac Mini hier eine Ausnahme dar. Der Computer kam in dieser Konfiguration erst kürzlich in den Handel. Umgerechnet bedeuten die 20 Prozent einen Angebotspreis von 835 Euro. Damit ist der Mac Mini 214 Euro günstiger als bei Apple selbst.
Doch wie gut ist dieser Preis im Vergleich zur Konkurrenz? Der Preisverlaufskurve von Idealo zufolge gab es den Mac Mini seit Marktstart noch nie günstiger. Derzeit bietet Amazon den Rechner also zum besten Preis im Netz an.
Fürs Geld bekommt ihr den Mac Mini mit M6-Prozessor, 16 Gigabyte Arbeits- und 256 Gigabyte SSD-Speicher. Zwar lässt sich die SSD nicht mehr händisch aufrüsten, weil Apple das Bauteil wieder verlötet hat. Es ist aber ganz einfach möglich, über die USB-C-Buchsen externen Speicher anzuschließen.

articles.title: Gemini 4: cuándo conviene usar Hydrogen y cuándo Neon, el modelo solo para suscriptores de pago
articles.text:
Google tiene dos modelos nuevos de su familia Gemini 4 al alcance del público: Hydrogen, disponible en todos los niveles de la app de Gemini, y Neon, que en la aplicación solo pueden elegir los suscriptores de los planes Google AI Pro y Ultra.
Los datos de esta guía provienen de los anuncios oficiales de Google. Las comparaciones de rendimiento son mediciones que la empresa presenta, en varios casos de índices externos que ella misma cita, y no han sido verificadas por este medio.
Qué ofrece cada modelo de Google
Según Google, Hydrogen está pensado para ejecutar tareas con rapidez. La empresa lo describe como un modelo para el trabajo diario: redactar correos, preparar guías de estudio, reescribir textos y armar tablas comparativas, con mayor fidelidad al tono y al formato que pida el usuario.
Neon apunta a trabajos de más exigencia. Google lo presenta para tareas de razonamiento complejo, como análisis de hojas de cálculo, lectura de PDF, gráficos y fotos, informes a partir de material denso y programación. Según la empresa, también puede traer datos de aplicaciones como Gmail y Documentos.
En el índice de inteligencia de Artificial Analysis, que Google cita en ambos anuncios, Hydrogen obtuvo 51 puntos en su nivel de razonamiento por defecto, uno más que Argon, otro modelo de la misma familia. Neon sumó 61 puntos en su nivel máximo, y Google lo ubica en el tercer lugar general de ese índice.
Quién puede elegir cada uno
Hydrogen está disponible para todos los niveles de la app de Gemini y del buscador de Google, de Google AI Studio (la herramienta de Google para probar sus modelos), de la interfaz de programación de Gemini y de Gemini para empresas. En Google Antigravity, su plataforma para programar con IA, solo lo tienen los suscriptores de pago Pro y Ultra.
Neon llegó en una primera etapa más restringida. En la app de Gemini, los suscriptores Pro y Ultra pueden seleccionarlo desde el menú desplegable de modelos. Para desarrolladores, está en el nivel de pago de la interfaz de programación en Google AI Studio, y las empresas lo usan desde la interfaz o ese mismo menú.
Google no indicó en los anuncios que Neon vaya a estar disponible para cuentas gratuitas de la app. Quien no tenga un plan Pro o Ultra, por lo tanto, no podrá elegirlo hoy, y la herramienta recomendada para ese usuario es Hydrogen.
Qué cambia en costo y razonamiento
Ambos modelos manejan una ventana de contexto de 1 millón de tokens, la cantidad de texto, imágenes o audio que pueden procesar de una vez. Para quienes pagan por uso de la interfaz de programación, Hydrogen cuesta USD 1,50 por millón de tokens de entrada y USD 7,50 por millón de salida, un precio fijo en toda la ventana de contexto.
Neon cuesta USD 3 por millón de tokens de entrada y USD 15 por millón de salida. Para texto ya procesado y guardado en memoria, que Google llama entrada en caché, la tarifa es de USD 0,15 por millón, un descuento del 95%.
Los dos modelos permiten ajustar cuánto razona la IA antes de responder. Hydrogen ofrece cuatro niveles: bajo, medio, alto (el predeterminado) y uno nuevo llamado xhigh. Neon también tiene cuatro. Un nivel más alto da respuestas más elaboradas, pero demora más y cuesta más en el uso por interfaz de programación.
Google afirma que Neon, en su nivel alto, cuesta 32% menos por tarea que Carbon, el modelo más grande de la familia que menciona el anuncio. En programación, la empresa añadió que Antigravity cuenta con una función llamada Orquestador, que cambia de modelo dentro de una misma sesión y puede usar Hydrogen para las tareas de ejecución.
Ante la duda, la lógica que surge de los anuncios es sencilla: Hydrogen para el trabajo de todos los días y para quien no paga una suscripción, y Neon para quien tiene un plan Pro o Ultra y necesita análisis más profundos. Esta guía rige para las versiones publicadas por Google el 12 y el 18 de noviembre de 2026.

articles.title: Lenovo Pro 9n review: 18-core RTX Spark in a fancy chassis
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
The Lenovo Pro 9n is an elegant consumer workstation with a vivid OLED screen and lots of ports, but it's expensive, and RTX Spark still needs to differentiate itself with Windows features to justify that price.
Reasons to buy
- + Vivid OLED screen
- + Two SSD slots
- + Lighter than Surface Laptop Ultra
- + Good port selection
Reasons to avoid
- - Too much software
- - ExpensiveBattery life could be better
- - Included stylus doesn't work on the touchscreen
- - Windows doesn't take advantage of RTX Spark
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test.
A lot of noise was made about the Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra, but there's a handful of other premium machines running Nvidia's new RTX Spark chips. Lenovo's Pro 9n follows Microsoft's lead, making a fancy laptop with its own touches, like an OLED panel and a stylus that works on the touchpad.
This is also our first time looking at the 18-core version of the RTX Spark, which has fewer CUDA cores than the last one we tested, so we'll see just what kind of changes in performance you get if you don't opt for a higher-end configuration.
Design of the Lenovo Pro 9n
The Lenovo Pro 9n is clearly a tool. It's a dark gray box with a Lenovo logo and a slight extrusion to fit Lenovo's signature anti-notch for the camera. The lid is flat, with a rounded keyboard deck, like many of Lenovo's premium Yoga laptops. It's a playful look that's less noticeable when the system is matte black rather than colorful.
The keyboard deck, including a massive touchpad, is logo-free other than an Nvidia RTX Spark sticker, which keeps all of your attention on the backlit keyboard and 15.3-inch OLED screen.
There are plenty of ports, and I appreciate that both sides of the laptop have both USB Type-C and Type-A. The left side also has HDMI and a 3.5 mm headphone jack, while the right side includes an SD card slot and an e-shutter for the webcam.
At 13.66 x 9.53 x 0.66 inches, this isn't a small system, but it's still one you can reasonably fit in your backpack. It's wider and deeper than the Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra (12.95 x 9.40 x 0.75 inches) but it's also thinner. Apple's new 16-inch MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR is a tad sleeker at 0.63 inches thick.
The Pro 9n measured in at 3.64 pounds pounds, less than 4.41-pound Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra. The 16-inch MacBook Pro is a bit heavier than the Pro 9n at 4.1 pounds.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Lenovo Pro 9n Specifications
| CPU | Nvidia RTX Spark (18-core CPU) | 
| Graphics | 5,120 CUDA cores, Blackwell-based | 
| Memory | 32GB LPDDR5X-9400 | 
| Storage | 1TB PCIe | 
| Display | 15.3-inch, 2560 x 1600, OLED, touch, 165 Hz | 
| Networking | MediaTek Wi-Fi 7 MT7925, Bluetooth 5.4 | 
| Ports | HDMI 2.1, 2s USB Type-A (10Gbps), 2x USB4 Type-C (40 Gbps), 3.5 mm headphone jack, SD card reader (UHS-II) | 
| Camera | 9.2 MP, IR, e-Shutter | 
| Battery | 92.5 WHr | 
| Power Adapter | 140W USB Type-C | 
| Stylus | Lenovo Yoga Pen Gen 2 | 
| Operating System | Windows 11 on Arm, Pro | 
| Dimensions (WxDxH) | 13.66 x 9.53 x 0.66 inches / 347 mm x 242 mm x 16.7 mm | 
| Weight | 3.64 pounds (1.65 kg) | 
| Price (as configured) | $3,249.99 | 
Productivity Performance on the Lenovo Pro 9n
The Lenovo Pro 9n features the lesser variant of the RTX Spark N1X, and this is our first look at a system with that config. This version has an 18-core CPU, down from the 20-core version we saw with the Surface Laptop Ultra. It also has 32GB of RAM and 1TB of storage.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
On Geekbench 6, the Pro 9n came in slightly behind the Surface Laptop in both single-core and multi-core performance (given how heavy the Surface Laptop is, some of this could come down to cooling). The MacBook Pro with M5 Max won out, while the Asus ZenBook A16 with Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme beat both RTX Sparks.
The Pro 9n copied 25GB of files at a rate of 1,205.37 MBps. That's not terrible, but in the ultra-premium price band, you can get faster speeds. Every other laptop beat the Pro 9n here.
On Handbrake, the Pro 9n transcoded a 4K video to 1080p in 2 minutes and 1 second, or 7 seconds behind the Surface Pro with the 20-core CPU. The Pro 9n beat the Snapdragon-powered Zenbook here.
We use Cinebench 2026 to stress test laptops, running a multi-core benchmark ten times in a row. The Pro 9n stayed largely consistent — in fact, it even got better later on, as the cooling kicked into high gear. The system started with a score of 6,219.85, and topped out on run 6 at 6,417.45. Most of the runs were in the high 6,300s. The RTX Spark's Cortex-A725 cores ran at an average of 2.81 GHz, while the Cortex-X925 cores averaged 3.57 GHz.
It's worth noting that HWinfo, which we used for monitoring, was missing a single A725 core. This also happened on the Surface Laptop Ultra, though now we can tell which cores are which.
AI Performance: Comparing the two RTX Sparks
The Lenovo Pro 9n we reviewed came with the entry-level version of Nvidia's RTX Spark, which has an 18-core CPU and 5,120 CUDA cores. It can be upgraded to a 20-core / 6,144 CUDA core chip in some configurations, which is the same chip we saw in the Surface Laptop Ultra.
To test the difference in AI performance, we ran AgentPerf-Local using Qwen 3.8-27B-UD_IQ3_XXS in order to fit in the limited available GPU memory (both are 32GB systems, with the Surface allowing 24GB of allocated graphics memory and the Pro 9n accepting just 16GB). The benchmark simulates running conversations by playing back conversations, with a majority of the work involving processing prompts rather than generating tokens.
The difference between the two RTX Spark systems wasn't particularly significant here. The Surface Laptop Ultra completed the benchmark in 1,148.3 seconds, while the Pro 9n took 1,196.6 seconds. That's a 4.12% difference in favor of the higher-end Spark.
Gaming and Graphics on the Lenovo Pro 9n
Beyond the difference in CPU cores, the version of RTX Spark in the Pro 9n we tested has 5,120 CUDA cores, down from 6,144 in the more powerful version in the Surface Laptop Ultra. (The beefier chip is also available in other configurations of the Pro 9n).
On 3DMark Steel Nomad, the Pro 9n earned a score of 2,796, falling behind the Laptop Ultra (4,355) and the MacBook Pro (3,865). It's still a more powerful system than the Zenbook with Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme (1,262).
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
In gaming, the RTX Spark isn't really meant for much above 1080p (perhaps 1440p, depending on the game). So in the case of our benchmarks, the difference in CUDA cores didn't have a stark difference, with nearly identical scores on Shadow of the Tomb Raider and Cyberpunk 2077. Far Cry 6, which is more CPU-focused, ran better on the 20-core RTX Spark.
When I played 007: First Light, with the game at 1920 x 1200 and settings on medium, and DLSS set to ultra performance, the game ran just over 30 frames per second. With DLSS on "dynamic," the game ran smoother, between 40 and 72 frames per second as Bond moved through a swanky hotel, though there was some jankiness to it. The game also took a long time to load, possibly due to Windows' Prism emulation.
Display on the Lenovo Pro 9n
The 15.3-inch OLED touchscreen on the Pro 9n is quite nice. The 165 Hz panel is vivid and bright enough for most uses.
The trailer for Artificial showed off the colors and blacks, as the trailer descends from lush greens outside of Sam Altman's home to a dark tunnel, until he arrives in a bunker with blue lights that all but jumped off the screen.
Lenovo's OLED panel was the most vivid of our test group on our colorimeter, covering 198% of the sRGB color space by volume, significantly higher than the rest of the field, though it often appeared oversaturated. In fact, it arrivees out of the box on its default wallpaper with severe pops of green and white. The MacBook Pro's PROLED XDR display has lower numbers on the colorimeter, but looks far more natural than what Lenovo is offering here.
At 440.6 nits of brightness, the Pro 9n's display is good, but the MacBook Pro has it beat at 529.5 nits, while the Surface Laptop Pro reached an astounding 944 nits in our testing.
Keyboard, Touchpad, and Stylus on the Lenovo Pro 9n
Lenovo's keyboard feels great. There's 1.5 mm of key travel, and you can feel it. It's deep, but punchy. The keycaps can be a bit slippery, though I typed at 106 words per minute on the monkeytype typing test, albeit with 2% less accuracy than usual.
The haptic touchpad is huge, smooth, and responsive. Oddly enough, despite being haptic, there is a noticeable depression when you click down, especially at the bottom edge. It's an odd feeling when you notice it, especially when you can still configure how hard you have to press in Windows to register a click.
Lenovo includes a stylus in the box for use with the touch screen, which is good for signing documents. The pen, however, does not work on the touchscreen, which is an odd choice. The Yoga Pen Gen 2 (typically sold for $63 with a case that isn't included here) can attach magnetically to the Pro 9n's lid and charges over USB Type-C, so you can use the same charger as the laptop. It supports up to 8,192 points of pressure sensitivity with AES3.0, or up to 4,096 points on other protocols.
Audio on the Lenovo Pro 9n
Lenovo's combination of two tweeters and two woofers does a decent job. They get nice and loud, easily filling a mid-sized office room with Justice's "Flower In A Hurricane."
The song's guitars and synths sounded excellent, as did SZA and Kevin Parker's voices. The drum beat was a bit low, but going into the Dolby Settings app, switching to the "Warm" music setting with boosted lows helped there.
Upgradeability on the Lenovo Pro 9n
There are 9 screws holding the bottom of the Lenovo Pro 9n on. The four closest to the hinge are longer than the remaining five, so be sure to keep them organized. You'll need a pry tool to remove the latches and release the base.
Inside, there's not a ton to repair or replace down the line for the average person. The 92.5 WHr battery is held in place with a few screws. You can also easily access the included M.2 2242 SSD, and there's a second bay for another drive of the same length. I would always prefer a more standard 2280 drive, but if this is what lets Lenovo fit two drives on the board (or at least give you the option to add a second drive), I'll take it.
The Wi-Fi card is soldered to the board and partially obscured by the heatsink's thick heat pipes.
Battery Life on the Lenovo Pro 9n
The Pro 9n ran for 10 hours and 30 minutes on average on our battery test, which browses the web, streams video from a server, and runs OpenGL tests with the screen set to 150 nits of brightness.
That's not too far off from other high-end Windows on Arm laptops, beating the Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme-based Zenbook A16 by 4 minutes, and it was 13 minutes behind the Surface Laptop Ultra with a more powerful version of N1X.
The MacBook Pro smoked them all though, running for 15 hours and 57 minutes on our test.
Heat on the Lenovo Pro 9n
During our Cinebench stress test, we took skin temperature measurements to get an idea of how hot the Pro 9n gets during use.
The center of the keyboard measured 98.5 degrees Fahrenheit, while the touchpad was 10 degrees cooler. The hottest point on the bottom of the laptop reached 101.5 F.
HWinfo hasn't been updated to be clear on which sensors are measuring what internally. We could make educated guesses, but we'll have more specifics when the software is updated.
Webcam on the Lenovo Pro 9n
The 9.2-megapixel webcam on the Pro 9n should be more than enough for video calling in 4K, assuming your software supports it. While making calls, I found that the camera captured fine details, like graying hairs on the side of my temples (it's been a long month).
The colors were a bit cool, however. I could do with more vibrancy and warmth to make it more realistic.
Software and Warranty on the Lenovo Pro 9n
There’s just too much pre-loaded software on the Pro 9n. The most important app is Vantage, a catch-all app with your serial number, user guides, warranty status, a number of device settings, and access to support services. But it also houses a ton of ads.
The company also has direct links in the Start menu and taskbar to the Lenovo subscription portal to buy software. An additional user guide is also in the start menu. There's also Smart Connect, to pair and transfer files between your laptop, tablet, and phone, along with a dashboard to view them all. The company also has its stylus settings app and a link in the Start Menu to its Artificial Intelligence policy, which looks more like an internal document than something meant for consumers.
Lenovo also includes some bloatware, like trials of McAfee antivirus and a promotional trial of Dropbox.
Like other RTX Spark systems, the Pro 9n is running Windows on Arm. It's better than it's ever been, but there are still times when it feels laggy. More games and apps than before are compatible, but it's still not perfect.
Lenovo sells the Pro 9n with a 1-year warranty, which can be extended with additional coverage for more money.
Lenovo Pro 9n Configurations
We tested the Lenovo Pro 9n in a $3,249.99 configuration with an 18-core RTX Spark CPU and integrated GPU using 5,120 CUDA cores, 32GB of RAM, a 1TB PCIe Gen 4 SSD, and Windows 11 Pro.
The cheapest version, at $2,999.99, uses the same processor and RAM as our review unit, comes with Windows 11 Home, and has 512GB of RAM.
Bumping up to the higher-end 20-core, 6,144 CUDA-core GPU costs an extra $450 but also gets you 64GB of RAM and 1TB of storage as a base. Moving to 128GB of RAM is $1,400, while moving to a 2TB PCIe Gen 5 SSD is another $450.
Bottom Line
The Lenovo Pro 9n is a minimalist, RTX Spark-based laptop with strong port selection and a lovely OLED screen. The keyboard has deep travel, and I don't mind a design that simply gets out of the way of your work.
Still, it's expensive, even with the base version of RTX Spark. Battery life is just past 10 hours, which I would like to see improve across the RTX Spark platform, and there aren't any AI features in Windows that make this chip special for anyone who isn't running local models.
If you are married to getting an RTX Spark machine, the Lenovo Pro 9n beats the Surface Laptop Ultra in three areas: It's lighter, has an OLED screen, and extra SSD slots (even if it is M.2 2242) for an upgrade down the line. Still, the Surface is a nicer, more premium design and has the fun, magnetic Surface Connect port.
Those who aren't running local models should probably be looking for a cheaper laptop. Those prioritizing battery life should consider a Mac. And those who like Windows on Arm can still consider Snapdragon X2, as Nvidia's entrance into this choppy sea should lift all ships.
Andrew E. Freedman is a senior editor at Tom's Hardware focusing on laptops, desktops and gaming. He also keeps up with the latest news. A lover of all things gaming and tech, his previous work has shown up in Tom's Guide, Laptop Mag, Kotaku, PCMag and Complex, among others. Follow him on Threads @FreedmanAE and BlueSky @andrewfreedman.net. You can send him tips on Signal: andrewfreedman.01

articles.title: Fin du système de réservation pour la Steam Machine 512 Go, la version 2 To retirée
articles.text:
Valve a décidé de revoir la procédure pour s'offrir la Steam Machine avec un accès plus simple à la version 512 Go, mais une drôle de surprise pour la mouture dotée d'un SSD de 2 To.
Après quelques mois, Valve a donc mis fin au système de réservation de sa Steam Machine. Il n'est plus nécessaire de rejoindre une file d'attente pour se payer la version 512 Go du mini-PC, mais la version 2 To ne semble plus devoir être soutenue par la marque américaine.
BenQ iScreenBar : la barre lumineuse qui s’accorde avec l’iMac
Des lignes en harmonie avec celles de l’ordinateur d’Apple, une conception rigoureuse, des matériaux sélectionnés, rien n’a été laissé au hasard, tout comme le service qu’elle rend une fois allumée !
Fin de partie pour la Steam Machine 2 To ?
Au moment de lancer la Steam Machine – son mini-PC pensé pour le salon –, Valve avait décidé de laisser le choix aux futurs clients : deux versions étaient ainsi mises sur le marché, avec comme seul changement la taille du SSD.
À un tout petit peu plus de 1 000 euros, on pouvait ainsi s'offrir une Steam Machine avec un espace de stockage minimaliste, seulement 512 Go pour l'unique SSD que la machine peut embarquer. Une version sensiblement mieux équipée, mais aussi nettement plus chère, était également proposée : dotée d'un SSD de 2 To, cette seconde mouture est facturée 1 359 euros ou, plutôt, était facturée 1 359 euros.
En effet, après quelques mois de distribution, Valve a décidé de complètement revoir la commercialisation de sa Steam Machine. La marque a expliqué ce changement dans une actualité publiée sur la plateforme Steam. La version 2 To semble plus compliquée à fabriquer pour Valve, qui a décidé de changer son statut à « en rupture de stock ». Il n'est plus non plus possible de s'inscrire sur la liste de réservation de ce modèle.
Notez au passage que sur la page magasin, c'est une autre mention qui est visible : « épuisée », pas bon signe. Valve souligne par ailleurs que « comme toujours, aucune unité n'est promise aux personnes se trouvant dans la file d'attente ». En d'autres termes, même en étant sur la fameuse liste d'attente, il n'est pas garanti que l'on puisse, un jour, être contacté par Valve pour acheter cette mouture 2 To.
La version 512 Go disponible sans attendre
En revanche, la mise à jour publiée par Valve n'est pas porteuse que de mauvaises nouvelles. En effet, il n'est plus non plus possible de s'inscrire sur la liste d'attente de la version 512 Go, mais pour une toute autre raison.
Comme Valve l'explique, « la Steam Machine 512 Go est désormais disponible à l'achat. Vous pouvez en acheter une directement en l'ajoutant au panier, dans la limite des stocks disponibles ». En d'autres termes, vous pouvez commander la Steam Machine 512 Go comme n'importe quel jeu Steam. La seule différence est qu'il faut tout de même attendre quelques jours pour qu'elle vous soit livrée : entre 6 et 10 jours d'après Steam.
Difficile cependant de savoir si c'est parce que la production a pris son rythme de croisière ou si c'est que la demande est aujourd'hui faible. Il est d'ailleurs intéressant de noter le second commentaire de Valve à propos de cette 512 Go : « si nous écoulons le stock actuel, le produit sera déclaré en rupture de stock, mais aucune autre file d'attente ne sera créée ». Clairement, la liste d'attente, c'est du passé pour la Steam Machine.
Se pose cependant la question de la continuité de la production alors que les ventes ne semblent pas décoller réellement. La question du tarif de la Steam Machine est évidemment dans tous les esprits, mais les prix de la DRAM et de la NAND ne fléchissent pas en cette fin d'année et ne donnent donc guère d'espoir sur une baisse de la Steam Machine, pourtant la seule manière de la voir décoller auprès des amateurs potentiels.
Source : Steam

articles.title: Sarvam clarifies AI strategy amid debate over hosting Chinese models
articles.text:
Sarvam clarifies AI strategy amid debate over hosting Chinese models
Co-founder Pratyush Kumar contends that a model’s country of origin and the location of the infrastructure on which it runs are two different matters. Building inference infrastructure does not take away from Sarvam’s core focus on developing its own models, he says.
After Sarvam AI’s Token Factory attracted both support and criticism, particularly over its inclusion of Chinese-developed AI models, co-founder Pratyush Kumar has sought to address the questions surrounding the platform’s funding, use of computing resources, and its relevance to Sarvam’s indigenous AI ambitions.
Kumar said the IndiaAI Mission offered around 20 startups access to graphics processing units (GPUs) at a 40% discount. Sarvam used this support to train its 105-billion-parameter model from scratch. He noted that the government did not fund Sarvam directly, with the subsidy instead going to GPU cloud providers.
Launched on November 16, Token Factory allows developers and businesses to access multiple AI models through a single application programming interface (API), with charges based on the number of tokens processed. Tokens are small units of text that an AI model reads or generates, while inference is the process of generating responses using a trained model.
The platform’s catalogue includes Sarvam’s own model alongside open-weight systems such as DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM and Google’s Gemma. Open-weight models make their trained parameters available for others to download and run.
Kumar emphasised that this business operates independently of the government-supported training effort. “We serve multiple open-weight models on GPUs we have privately procured, without any government support,” he said. Sarvam has also said that its subsidised compute allocation ended in March 2026.
The inclusion of Chinese-developed models has fuelled the debate over technological sovereignty. Sarvam’s position is that a model’s country of origin and the location of the infrastructure on which it runs are two different matters. Hosting open-weight models on Indian GPUs means prompts need not be sent to overseas model providers.
However, domestic hosting does not make a foreign-developed model Indian or transfer its intellectual property. Nor does it, by itself, resolve concerns about software supply chains and model behaviour.
Sarvam says zero data retention, under which prompts and responses are not stored, is available on request, while operational logs are governed separately. Data residency alone is not a complete privacy guarantee.
Kumar maintained that building inference infrastructure does not take away from Sarvam’s core focus on developing its own models. On November 22, the company announced Sarvam-105B-1711, an updated open-weight version of its 105B model, claiming improvements in reasoning, tool use, and Indian-language performance.
Sarvam noted that the model’s average score across eight benchmarks for conversational agents had risen from 42.6 to 73.9. Kumar also indicated further releases across vision, speech and edge AI, alongside efforts to secure more advanced computing infrastructure for training larger models.
The commercial opportunity highlights a wider industry shift. As AI becomes part of everyday applications, the cost of running models repeatedly can matter as much as the cost of developing them. Sarvam is not alone in pursuing this market.
Other Indian players, including L&T, Jarvislabs, Utho Labs and Mirror Security, are also developing similar offerings, competing with established global providers such as Together AI and Fireworks AI.
This activity is unfolding alongside government efforts to strengthen domestic AI capabilities. The IndiaAI Mission, approved in 2024 with a five-year outlay of about Rs 10,372 crore, supports foundation-model development and shared computing infrastructure. A July government update said 20 indigenous model proposals had been identified and 93 lakh GPU hours sanctioned across 237 projects.
Edited by Swetha Kannan

articles.title: La nueva guerra fría entre Estados Unidos y China no es por los chips: es por los monos de laboratorio
articles.text:
En el campo de la investigación biomédica, los monos son fundamentales para poder realizar experimentación y probar, por ejemplo, medicamentos antes de pasar al testeo con humanos. Hasta hace unos años, China era uno de los mayores exportadores de los macacos cangrejeros que compraban en Estados Unidos para realizar su experimentación. Pero la pandemia de COVID-19 rompió ese equilibrio en cuestión de semanas, dando un gran giro al tablero.
El cambio. Hasta finales de la década pasada, Estados Unidos dependía de China para abastecer buena parte de sus centros de investigación, que utilizan alrededor de 60.000 primates no humanos cada año. Y para suplir esta demanda, por ejemplo, se compró en 2019 un total de 20.270 primates.
Pero todo cambió en enero de 2020, puesto que con el estallido de la crisis sanitaria del coronavirus, Pekín prohibió el comercio de animales salvajes alegando riesgos para la salud pública. Algo que tuvo un impacto directo puesto que en 2020 las importaciones estadounidenses de primates desde China se desplomaron un 81,6 %, mientras que las procedentes de Camboya se dispararon un 82,8 %, alcanzando los 15.664 ejemplares en el año fiscal 2020.
China quiere más. El cierre de fronteras no significó que China hubiera perdido el interés en los macacos, sino que necesitaban redirigirlos hacia sus propios laboratorios. Y tiene todo el sentido puesto que el país atraviesa una expansión biomédica sin precedentes que ha terminado provocando un cuello de botella interno al necesitar cada vez más animales de experimentación.
Y para cubrir este déficit, Pekín salió a comprar fuera, puesto que, según los datos recopilados por Science, las importaciones chinas de monos pasaron de poco más de 2.400 ejemplares en 2023 a superar los 13.000 en 2025, siendo el principal proveedor Camboya.
El blanqueo de monos. El repentino protagonismo de Camboya como granero mundial de primates arrastra un historial judicial y ambiental espinoso. En noviembre de 2022, el Departamento de Justicia de Estados Unidos acusó formalmente a ocho personas de integrar una red que habría "blanqueado" hasta 3.000 macacos capturados en la naturaleza desde al menos diciembre de 2017. Según los fiscales federales, los animales pasaban por las instalaciones de la empresa Vanny Bio Research para ser etiquetados falsamente como nacidos en cautividad antes de su exportación.
Y aunque estas acusaciones quedaron en la nada, la realidad es que las dudas sobre la trazabilidad de estos animales nunca se han disipado. Y es que son varios los informes que cuestionan que las granjas de crías camboyanas tuvieran capacidad biológica real para reproducir macacos cangrejeros al ritmo que declaraban en sus certificados.
Buscando otros socios. Tras el escándalo judicial de 2022, las importaciones estadounidenses desde Camboya quedaron prácticamente paralizadas y los proveedores tuvieron que diversificar sus compras hacia países como Mauricio o Vietnam.
En paralelo, la política científica en Washington ha dado un giro significativo hacia la reducción de la experimentación animal. En abril de 2025, la Administración Trump impulsó diferentes medidas, como por ejemplo el retirar la obligatoriedad de ensayar determinados fármacos en animales, como ocurre con los anticuerpos monoclonales. Pero no se queda aquí, ya que los Institutos Nacionales de Salud comunicaron que recortaría también el uso de animales en las investigaciones que financian.
Una guerra comercial. En los laboratorios, el temor es que la geopolítica termine estrangulando las líneas de investigación básica que aún no tienen un sustituto viable. "Necesitamos estabilizar y fortalecer el proceso académico, incluido el acceso a primates no humanos para la investigación", sostiene Paul Nuyujukian, neurólogo de la Universidad de Stanford cuyo equipo emplea macacos para desarrollar interfaces cerebro-máquina destinadas a pacientes con ictus o epilepsia.
Y este choque de intereses es lo que verdaderamente preocupa a los expertos. Y es que si Washington y Pekín empiezan a percibir a los primates de investigación como un activo estratégico limitado, se podría desencadenar una guerra comercial de monos, lo que podría intensificar el tráfico ilegal de estos animales para poder seguir con la investigación al máximo nivel.

articles.title: How Notable Capital, GIC, and Baillie Gifford bet big on Anthropic before its IPO | TechCrunch
articles.text:
When Notable Capital poured roughly 10% of the U.S. portion of its $1 billion-plus fund into Anthropic’s Series E, many limited partners were perplexed by the massive bet. Claude’s maker was still trailing its biggest rival, OpenAI, and DeepSeek had released its R1 model just weeks earlier, threatening to overtake closed-source competitors. Moreover, at $61.5 billion, Anthropic’s valuation was by far the highest that the predominantly early-stage venture firm had invested at in its 25-year history.
But investors at Notable, formerly known as GGV Capital before its 2024 split from its China operations, were confident in Anthropic’s future. A team that included managing partners Hans Tung and Glenn Solomon and principal Dan Cahana crunched the numbers and found that developers were increasingly favoring Claude over ChatGPT, using Claude 70% of the time, a reversal from the previous year.
“We just knew that for AI, the developer is at the center because they’re the early adopters,” Tung, a co-founder of the firm, told TechCrunch.
Having navigated the complexities of U.S.-China relations firsthand, Notable was also convinced that “mission-critical” work would always require U.S.-based, closed-source models, Tung said.
Less than two years later, Notable’s LPs are no longer questioning the outsized investment. On Wednesday, Anthropic raised $81.3 billion in the largest IPO in history, reaching a fully diluted valuation of about $1.5 trillion before its shares began trading the next day, a paper return of roughly 15 times.
Notable is, of course, not the only firm sitting on a massive paper windfall from Anthropic. Even traditional late-stage investors, who rarely see venture-scale multiples, are set for a big win.
Singaporean sovereign wealth fund GIC had been researching Anthropic throughout 2024, but it didn’t make its first investment until after Chris Emanuel, head of the fund’s tech investments, met with Anthropic CFO Krishna Rao at Che Fico, an Italian restaurant in San Francisco, in early 2025. Rao helped pique Emanuel’s interest in the company by showing that model improvements were driving rising enterprise adoption. GIC then made its first investment in Anthropic’s Series F, a round announced in September 2025 at a $183 billion valuation.
“Claude Code was just released then,” Emanuel told TechCrunch. “It was very early, but even then, we could see signs that it was really popular with developers.” GIC’s conviction in the AI lab was so high that the fund later led Anthropic’s Series G alongside Coatue at a $380 billion valuation, and returned as one of the co-leads for the pre-IPO round at $965 billion. Across the three rounds, GIC invested more than $4.5 billion in Anthropic, amassing a stake equal to about 1% of the company after its IPO, according to a person familiar with GIC’s financials.
Lilian Li, who leads U.S. growth investments at Baillie Gifford, began studying Anthropic and speaking with its team nearly two years before first investing in the company’s Series F. Baillie Gifford invested in the Claude maker once it became clear that the company was “executing consistently” on its vision while generating strong revenue and “compelling gross margins,” Li told TechCrunch.
After Baillie Gifford’s initial investment, Anthropic continued to deliver on its promises, expanding into industries such as legal services and life sciences, as well as broader applications like Cowork and cybersecurity, Li said.
“It’s actually quite incredible how consistent they have been with how quickly everything’s been changing,” she added. Baillie Gifford went on to invest a total of $1.5 billion across three funding rounds, a bet that has generated substantial paper gains for the investment manager, as well as for dozens of other backers who invested at what once seemed like astronomical valuations.

articles.title: I put the best headphones from Apple, Technics, Bowers & Wilkins and Nothing in group test to find my ultimate winner — and the result may surprise you
articles.text:
I tested four of the best wireless noise-canceling headphones in 2026, and there's only one pair I’d buy on Black Friday
Four of 2026's best wireless headphones, tested side by side to find a winner
It has been an absolute barnstormer year for over-ear headphones. I’ve personally reviewed several of the best noise-canceling headphones of 2026 — and I even put two of them head-to-head in my Apple AirPods Max 2 vs. Bowers & Wilkins Px8 S2 showdown, a few months after the AirPods' March release.
Now, (and with Black Friday around the corner; see those early Black Friday deals landing as I type, like apples from a tree) I think we need to extend the group test to include four key models you're likely to see discounts on this peak sales season.
Fortunately, I reviewed (or, in two cases, helped test) all four sets of headphones, and I've got them here in front of me now for a group showdown.
Under direct comparison, I'm going to tell you which feels best on, looks best, sounds the most faithfully detailed, lasts the longest, and is the easiest to use — because maybe you're buying for someone not quite so tech-savvy, and giving them a gift they'll love using is a perfectly valid, kind concern (so well done on that).
All four models earned glowing 5-star or 4.5-star ratings under TechRadar's rigorous review process, so they're all very good indeed. A part of me knows that whichever you pick, you won't be disappointed. Then again, my modus operandi as TechRadar's Audio Editor is getting you the ideal set of cans for you or whomever you're buying for.
So let's work out which of this quartet of cans that is, shall we? Meet the players: 
Apple AirPods Max 2; unveiled March 16, 2026 — $549 / £499 / AU$999
Technics EAH-A1000; unveiled September 29, 2026 — $449 / £399 / AU$699
Nothing Headphone (a); unveiled March 13, 2026 — $199 / £149 / AU$329
Bowers & Wilkins Px8 S2; unveiled September 24, 2025 — $799 / £629 / AU$1,299
Now, let's go…
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Design, comfort and battery life
We're not messing around here — time is of the essence. The easiest thing is to list the cans, with their perks and shortfalls, succinctly and directly. So here it is folks…
Apple AirPods Max 2
The good: without a doubt, the most comfortable of the quartet — despite being the heaviest, at 386.2g. The mesh headband may look a little bizarre, but it distributes weight beautifully across the crown of the head and, as someone who experiences migraines complete with auras (don't even get me started), comfort is an important thing to note. Another highlight is the Digital Crown volume roller on the top right earcup. Clamping force is gentle but effective, and the ear cups, while big, are relatively nice and close to the ear. 
The bad: you only get up to 20 hours of stamina (with ANC enabled), which is the worst battery life in this roundup. Also, that case is possibly the flimsiest and easiest to lose of the lot.
Bowers & Wilkins Px8 S2
The good: emphatically the most winsome and elite-looking of the bunch and yes, they're also comfortable. There’s just the right amount of memory foam beneath the headband (which is also renewable or replaceable, by a qualified technician — a nice touch given the considerable asking fee). Despite the ample sprinkling of burnished aluminum and even a flourish of exposed cable detail on the yokes, they weigh just 310g too. Unlike AirPods above, you get aptX Adaptive and aptX Lossless codec support, if you're an Android owner with access to music files of quality. 
The bad: battery life is a little better than the AirPods Max at 30 hours with ANC on, but it's far from the best here. The build also features Nappa leather, so they're no good for vegetarians. The hard-shell case feels premium, but can feel a tad large because these cans lie flat but do not fold.
Nothing Headphone (a)
The good: given that they're by far the cheapest in this group test, at $199 / £149 / AU$329, there's an awful lot to love about the build quality, which weighs 310g (like the B&W above) and, like the above two models, also supports USB-C wired audio. Unlike the two picks above, you get LDAC support here (great for Sony and Samsung handset owners), and the on-ear controls have no business being this good at this level. In particular, the roller for volume control is exceptional and makes other solutions feel crude by comparison. Then, there's the 'rocker' control underneath, which is also beautifully intuitive for track skips. Top it off with a round multi-function custom button and if it's easy-to-use you want, these are the cans. Oh, and I haven't mentioned stamina! At up to 135 hours, it's superb. OK, that's with ANC off, but still, we're looking at class-leading here. 
The bad: these aren't cans for the clumsy: you only get a flimsy pouch to put them in, which doesn't bode well for bag slingers.
Technics EAH-A1000
The good: the lightest in the roundup, at 306g, but they never ever look or feel flimsy — and comfort levels are spot on. Also, the 'leather' is vegan, which is a big tick for those who only support vegan products. These headphones are understatedly elegant and, with up to 45 hours with ANC on or up to 90 hours with ANC off, they're on the money there too. While the ear cups do protrude a fair way, the 18-degree angle was particularly comfortable for me, a woman — and indeed, the design engineer here is a woman, so depending on whom you're buying these for, worth considering. Again, there's USB-C wired audio support, and Technics' magnetic fluid driver tech is a first in this over-ear category. The case? It's hard-shell, bijou, and quite beautiful.
The bad: the downside here is the on-ear controls. They're physical buttons, and while acceptable in use, they do occasionally fail to register presses. In direct comparison to others in this roundup, they're not as reliable for playback, volume handling, and powering off.
- Design/aesthetics winner: Bowers & Wilkins Px8 S2
- Comfort winner: Apple AirPods Max 2
- Stamina winner: Nothing Headphone (a)
Features and ANC
Apple AirPods Max 2
The good: if you have an iPhone, the ANC here is unmatched. Apple has made these headphones ideal for the iOS ensconced — and to that end, if you've got a newer iPhone with Apple Intelligence, you get Live Translation. You can deploy it easily, via the Digital Crown and it is exceptional for travellers. Also exceptional is Apple's Spatial Audio with head-tracking, and if you don't believe me, grab an iPad and stream the movie Gravity using Apple's head-tracked spatial side-sauce. See? Also, the Conversation Awareness perk (pipe up and the music pipes down and transparency kicks in, so you'll hear whatever was just said to you) is a winner all day long. 
The bad: Don't have an iPhone? You'll need to move on I fear — you really aren't getting them at their best with an Android phone. Also perhaps worth noting is that even with an iPhone, you won't get Apple's earbuds-only heart-rate monitoring or hearing tests to generate the Cupertino giant's hearing-aid-like features.
Bowers & Wilkins Px8 S2: 
The good: these headphones are not overly stuffed with extraneous features (no live translation, hearing tests or gesture support here) but what they do, they do well — and there's beauty in the detail. The Wear Sensing feature, for example, makes for a truly natural headphone experience, pausing and resuming your music simply by lifting either earpiece on or off your ear. It sounds simple but when it works this well, you'll never want cans without it.
The bad: the ANC here is fine, rather than fantastic — and while they shine in other areas, at this price we are allowed to be a little pickier. Also, True Immersion (B&W's spatial audio offering) is acceptable, rather than truly awesome.
Nothing Headphone (a) 
The good: for the money, the ANC is spot on. It's not AirPods Max 2 good, but that's hardly fair given they're less than half the price of those. What you will get is a few fun device-agnostic ways to enhance the sound, including an AI Dynamic Bass Enhancement option, plus two device-neutral Spatial Audio modes (Concert or Cinema) to enhance your source material. Neither option includes dynamic head tracking but they still add depth and value to the proposition. 
The bad: there's no auto-pause feature (also called wearer detection) to halt playback when you take them off. It's a shame — it's relatively standard even in affordable cans now.
Technics EAH-A1000
The good: there's wearer detection to pause your music, plus ANC that can either be set to 'Adaptive', to automatically adjust, or simply 'On' to tweak manually as you move to busier environments. This is done on a little virtual dial within the easy-to-navigate (and easy-to-tailor) Technics AudioConnect app. For me, dialling up the ANC to 100% or thereabouts gives very good results — better than the B&W and Nothing options, if not quite as good as AirPods. Also competent is the spatial audio offering, which can be deployed head-tracking. It's a more subtle effect than with AirPods Max but still, it absolutely deserves merit. 
The bad: you'll get no hearing tests, hearing aid perks or scope for nodding to summon your voice assistant here and while I perhaps don't miss these features, it's my job to note their absence. Also, the Transparency profile felt a little undercooked — I could use more help to hear external sounds.
- Features winner: 
iOS — Apple AirPods Max 2
Android — Nothing Headphone (a)
- ANC winner: 
iOS — AirPods Max 2
Android — Technics EAH A1000
Sound quality
Apple AirPods Max 2: expect an expansive, unfurled sound with bass frequencies that rumble, snap and boom. Timing, too, is exceptional. I dare you to stream Bad Bunny's Tití Me Preguntó and not dance.
For crisp leading edges of notes and an extra ounce of detail, you'll get just a touch more insight and loyalty to the original recording from the Bowers & Wilkins Px8 S2, but AirPods Max 2's Spatial Audio beats B&W's True Immersion, with the latter coming off a little veiled in direct comparison. This is a fun, zealous, expansive listen and no mistake.
Bowers & Wilkins Px8 S2: if you buy these headphones, let it be for their detailed, faithful, neutral, critical sound quality, dear reader. Turning all ANC and extras off, it’s hard to lay a glove on the Bowers & Wilkins Px8 S2 in this key area. Where they really excel, they leave their nominal competition for dust. The size and coherence of the soundstage they create is class-leading; the dynamic nuance is like the hand of a skilled surgeon; the forensic level of insight is nothing short of superb. If it’s scale, variation and detail you want from your headphones, you've just found your ideal set — if your budget can stretch to them.
Nothing Headphone (a) 
The spaciousness here runs rings around Nothing's inaugural July 2025-issue Headphone (1) although I know that comparison isn't why we're here. The midrange expresses itself beautifully, but the treble never feels like it's pushing to compete in the mix. If anything, the opposite is true: there is a marginal softness of detail or roundness to the Headphone (a)'s sound. Don't get me wrong, they are not poor for the money, but if your budget stretches further, better sound can be had higher up the food chain. Switch to any other headphone in this roundup and crisper leading edges of notes can be yours. I know, it stands to reason that an expensive thing will sound better than a cheaper thing (and lo! It has come to pass) but still, it's my job to point that out. 
Technics EAH-A1000
If you need exceptionally detailed audio, with expanse and no musical passage left behind, overshadowed or ignored, these are your headphones. For lovers of an integrated, neutral hi-fi sound in headphones that can be used to dig out extra sonic surprises in their higher-resolution music files, these headphones won't disappoint. But there's a downside: they also very occasionally come off a little too polite and lacking in bite and excitement — it's marginal, but it's there. Nothing in Technics' headphones is ever over-emphasised or bloated, but in making sure they never offend, sometimes they're a little too mild-mannered for my listening taste. 
- Sound quality winner: Bowers & Wilkins Px8 S2
The overall winner (as Black Friday approaches, fast)
Oh it's a tough one, isn't it? In fact, I cannot give you a one product answer, since these cans are all the best — in certain areas.
But while I can't give you a simple "it's these, no question" answer, I can give you concrete answers. My succinct-as-I-can-make-it verdict is this: for stonkingly good sound above all else, you need to be going for the Bowers & Wilkins Px8 S2.
If ANC and/or Spatial Audio performance is your top priority, it's got to be the AirPods Max 2 — provided you've got an iPhone (if not, allow me to nudge you towards the Bose QuietComfort Ultra Headphones Gen 2, for similar money).
For detailed neutrality and a superbly chic, comfortable, beautiful design (especially for a female wearer; perhaps one who adores classical or acoustic music) look to the Technics EAH-A1000.
And if battery-life is at the very top of your checklist, do not overlook the Nothing Headphone (a) — because this is the set that will still be playing long after the other three headphones in this list have had to go for a charge…

articles.title: Actuellement noté 4,5/5, ce smartphone Samsung perd 315,17 € pour le Black Friday 2026
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 : Le smartphone Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra 256 Go à 869,99 € (-27%)
À l'occasion du Black Friday, le Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra passe à 869,99 € chez Boulanger.com, soit une baisse d'environ 27 % et une économie de 315,17 €. Porté par son écran très lumineux et sa solide autonomie, ce smartphone affiche une note actuelle de 4,5/5 au sein de notre rédaction.
Samsung a conçu le Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra pour incarner le sommet de son catalogue, tant sur le plan matériel que logiciel. Par rapport au Galaxy S24 Ultra, ce smartphone très haut de gamme gagne encore en puissance et en endurance pour offrir une utilisation sans ralentissement. L'appareil avait convaincu notre laboratoire lors de son passage sur le banc d'essai.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, le terminal descend à 869,99 € chez Boulanger.com, soit environ 27 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours (1 185,16 €). Cela représente une économie de 315,17 € sur ce modèle.
Un écran très lumineux et une configuration solide
Le smartphone de Samsung mise d'abord sur son confort de lecture avec une dalle de 6,9 pouces affichant une définition de 3120 x 1440 pixels, particulièrement lisible en plein jour grâce à sa forte luminosité. Sous le capot, le processeur Snapdragon 8 Elite assure une réactivité sans faille pour faire tourner les applications lourdes et les jeux exigeants. Comme nous l'avons souligné dans notre test complet, l'appareil affiche actuellement la note de 4,5/5 et confirme ses aptitudes haut de gamme au quotidien.
Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra
Points forts
- Écran ultra lumineux.
- Performances de haute volée.
- Excellente autonomie.
- Polyvalence photo et vidéo.
Points faibles
- Charge que l'on aimerait plus rapide.
- S Pen sans Bluetooth.
NB : La baisse de prix rapportée est calculée en comparant le prix le plus bas du jour avec la moyenne des prix les plus bas pratiqués par tous les marchands pour le produit le mois dernier, avec des règles de sécurité pour écarter les prix des boutiques dont la politique en matière de TVA n’est pas claire (dites boutiques “grises”, typiquement en cas d’import de Chine).
Une grande endurance malgré une charge perfectible
Avec sa batterie de 5000 mAh et sa certification IP68 (étanche à l'eau et à la poussière), le téléphone offre une excellente autonomie pour tenir de longues journées d'activité sans craindre les immersions accidentelles. Au rayon des regrets, la vitesse de charge reste en retrait par rapport aux cadors du secteur et demandera un peu de patience aux utilisateurs les plus pressés. Le stylet S Pen fait aussi l'impasse sur la connectivité Bluetooth, ce qui prive l'utilisateur de certaines commandes à distance sans toutefois gêner la prise de notes directe sur l'écran.
Xiaomi 17 : l'autre option face au Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra
Le Xiaomi 17 propose une approche différente en misant sur un format plus compact tout en intégrant une charge rapide plus efficace. Actuellement noté 5/5 par notre rédaction, il profite lui aussi d'une autonomie longue durée et d'un écran bien calibré au quotidien.
Le modèle de Xiaomi est vendu 130,01 € moins cher que le Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra à son prix du jour, mais le smartphone de Samsung conserve l'avantage d'un affichage de 6,9 pouces plus spacieux pour le multimédia.
Xiaomi 17
Points forts
- Écran ultra lumineux.
- Bonne autonomie.
- Grand-angle réussi.
- Format compact plaisant.
Points faibles
- De la chauffe.
- Ultra grand-angle décevant.

articles.title: Cómo hablar con Gemini desde la pantalla del auto con CarPlay en un iPhone
articles.text:
Los usuarios de iPhone pueden conversar con Gemini Live, el modo de voz del asistente de inteligencia artificial de Google, desde la pantalla de Apple CarPlay. Google anunció que el despliegue ya es global y alcanza a todos los usuarios de Gemini en iOS, en cada idioma que admite Gemini Live.
Para activarlo hay tres requisitos previos, según el anuncio de la empresa: tener la app de Gemini actualizada a la última versión en el iPhone, habilitar el permiso de micrófono y haber usado Gemini Live en el teléfono al menos una vez.
Los pasos para empezar a usarlo
Con esos requisitos cumplidos, el proceso es corto. Primero, hay que abrir la tienda de aplicaciones del iPhone y actualizar Gemini. Después, en los ajustes del teléfono o cuando la app lo pida, se concede el acceso al micrófono.
El tercer paso es abrir Gemini en el teléfono e iniciar una conversación con Gemini Live, aunque sea una prueba breve. Google lo exige antes de usar la función en el auto.
Luego, al conectar el iPhone al auto, se toca el ícono de Gemini en la pantalla de CarPlay o en su barra lateral. Desde allí se puede retomar una conversación reciente o empezar una nueva, según la descripción de Google.
La empresa indica que el servicio funciona como una charla de ida y vuelta: el usuario puede interrumpir para añadir un detalle, cambiar de tema o hacer una pausa cuando necesita concentrarse en una salida de la ruta.
Qué se le puede pedir mientras se maneja
Google propone cuatro usos. El primero es preparar el día: preguntar qué hay en la agenda, a qué hora conviene salir hacia la próxima cita o ensayar lo que se dirá en una reunión. Entre los ejemplos de la empresa figura la frase “¿Cómo se ve mi día?”.
El segundo es repasar el correo. Como Gemini se conecta con las aplicaciones de Google Workspace, como Gmail y Google Calendar, permite pedir un resumen diario, un repaso de los mensajes sin leer, una síntesis de hilos largos y la redacción de una respuesta usando solo la voz.
El tercero son las recomendaciones locales, desde un lugar rápido para almorzar en la zona de destino hasta la historia de un monumento. El cuarto es pensar en voz alta: ensayar una presentación, preparar una conversación difícil o pedir que se explique un tema complejo en términos simples.
Todo lo que se hable en CarPlay se sincroniza con la app del iPhone. Según Google, los resúmenes, las notas y las ideas quedan en el historial de chats cuando el conductor estaciona.
Lo que el anuncio no aclara
El comunicado no menciona el precio ni la versión mínima de iOS, ni qué modelos de auto o de iPhone son compatibles y tampoco precisa si hay límites de uso. Esos datos no figuran en el anuncio de Google.
La empresa presenta la función como una extensión de lo que ya ofrecía en Android Auto y en los autos con Google integrado. Su descripción se centra en conversaciones con las manos libres y la vista en el camino.
El despliegue comenzó el 11 de noviembre y, según el anuncio, llega de forma gradual a todos los usuarios de Gemini en iOS. Quien no vea el ícono debe confirmar que la app esté actualizada y que haya usado Gemini Live en el teléfono.
Android Auto cambia su diseño
Google ajusta Android Auto en dos frentes. Ya retiró el soporte por cable para Android 9 y 10: el mínimo ahora es Android 11, según detectó ZDNET. La compatibilidad va hasta Android 17, y también se requiere plan de datos, cable USB adecuado y un estéreo compatible (Android Go queda excluido).
En paralelo, avanza en secreto el rediseño interno llamado “Cielo”. Las versiones 18.0 y 18.1 no muestran cambios visibles, pero esconden pistas: un recurso llamado cielo_launcher para alternar apps como Google Maps y Spotify, animaciones nuevas, ajustes de modo claro/oscuro para Samsung y escalado de mapas, según 9to5Google.
El proyecto, mostrado en Google I/O, sumará widgets y el lenguaje visual Material 3 Expressive, aunque sin fecha de lanzamiento confirmada.

articles.title: GLP-1 drugs could have a surprisingly large environmental payoff
articles.text:
GLP-1 weight-loss medicines such as Ozempic and Wegovy could affect much more than the waistlines of the people who take them. If widely used, our new research suggests these appetite-suppressing medicines could transform the global food system and free up vast areas of agricultural land.
The global food system is ultimately driven by demand. If people eat less, producers respond, affecting production, prices, trade, and how much land is needed. We used a powerful computer simulation to explore scenarios ranging from GLP-1 use concentrated in high-income countries to widespread global access.
With widespread use of these medicines among adults living with obesity, we estimate that reduced calorie intake could prevent up to 6.6 million deaths each year by 2050, while freeing up as much as 32 million hectares of agricultural land—an area slightly larger than Italy—for other uses.
The biggest effects, however, occurred when reduced calorie intake was combined with a shift toward healthier diets. In this scenario, up to 7 million deaths could be avoided each year by 2050, while around 46 million hectares of agricultural land would have become available for other uses. This suggests that alongside weight-loss medicines, we need to make healthier options more widely available, affordable, and more appealing.
The food system could respond in unexpected ways
Food systems are interconnected across countries. If demand falls in one part of the world, this can affect farming, trade, and food prices elsewhere, with consequences for people who are not taking the medications at all.
Lower demand from GLP-1 users, for instance, could make food cheaper. That sounds positive, but cheaper food could also encourage greater consumption among non-users, offsetting some of the intended benefit. The effects of widespread GLP-1 use, in other words, cannot be understood just by looking at individual patients’ weight loss. They ripple through the global food system.
It’s tempting to read these findings as an argument for putting more people on weight-loss medication. That would miss the bigger picture.

articles.title: ‘You Can See Everything’ has made more than $100M worldwide | TechCrunch
articles.text:
“You Can See Everything,” Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s documentary about Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes, reached an impressive box office milestone this weekend, becoming one of the few documentaries to make more than $100 million worldwide.
Variety reports that almost all of the film’s $102.4 million box office has come from U.S. audiences, from whom it has grossed $93.4 million so far.
“You Can See Everything” will be opening in many more countries over the next few months — starting with Mexico, Brazil and Argentina on Nov. 25 and 26 — so its box office total could end up significantly higher.
And while the documentary was already an undeniable commercial success for indie studio A24 (especially with a reported budget of $7 million), it could now surpass the records set by the highest grossing documentaries of all time — “March of the Penguins” ($127 million globally) and “Fahrenheit 9/11” ($222 million globally).

articles.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (November 23, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: Daily roundup (November 23, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Monday, November 23, 2026.
From Sridhar Vembu's view on AI to Government of Karnataka training AI talent, YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors.
Latest News
What mechanisation and automation did to farmers, weavers, carpenters and ironsmiths could now be happening to mathematicians and programmers, according to Zoho co-founder Sridhar Vembu.
He believes artificial intelligence (AI) is beginning to displace work traditionally associated with highly skilled intellectual professionals, just as earlier technological advances transformed occupations built around manual skills and craftsmanship.
In a post on X, Vembu backed an observation by AI researcher Subbarao Kambhampati that the intellectual class had largely been spared the loss of purpose experienced by workers displaced by previous technological revolutions.
Pegasystems partners with Govt of Karnataka to build AI talent
Enterprise AI software company Pegasystems Inc is collaborating with the Department of IT & BT, Government of Karnataka as the state seeks to expand its technology talent pool and strengthen its position as an AI innovation hub.
The collaboration supports the government’s broader industry partnership to train students and engineers across the state of Karnataka. As part of this effort, Pegasystems will train and certify an initial cohort of 200 candidates in 2027. The training will take place across three to four clusters in Karnataka, giving participants industry-relevant skills and hands-on expertise.
Other news
MobiKwik’s Zaakpay goes live with Visa Payment Passkey
One MobiKwik Systems Limited announced that Zaakpay, its RBI-authorised online payment aggregator, has gone live with Visa Payment Passkey, enabling merchants on its platform to offer eligible Visa cardholders a simpler authentication experience at online checkout.
The feature allows customers to authenticate eligible online card transactions using their device's built-in security, without having to wait for or enter an SMS OTP (one-time password).
Visa Payment Passkey allows customers to complete eligible online card transactions using the security features built into their devices. Following a one-time registration, customers can use their passkey to authenticate eligible payments across participating merchants checkouts.
University of Liverpool Bengaluru, Biocon Academy explore partnerships
The University of Liverpool Bengaluru and Biocon Academy jointly organised a roundtable bringing together senior leaders from academia, healthcare, biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, and clinical research to explore opportunities for strengthening UK-India collaboration in education, research, healthcare innovation and workforce development.
The roundtable provided a platform for industry and academic stakeholders to discuss potential partnerships across the life sciences sector.
Discussions explored opportunities to leverage the University of Liverpool's expertise in drug discovery, women's health, artificial intelligence, and clinical trials alongside India's strengths in biotechnology and pharmaceutical manufacturing.

articles.title: Paso a paso para invertir en criptomonedas y cuál es su valor este domingo 22 de noviembre
articles.text:
Las criptomonedas son un activo digital innovador que han experimentado un crecimiento monumental en los últimos tiempos debido a varios elementos que contribuyen a ello, entre ellos que algunos gobiernos hayan decidido darles una oportunidad como moneda de curso legal; no obstante, también han sufrido descalabros que han puesto en duda su viabilidad, como el más reciente episodio conocido como el "criptoinvierno".
Pese a este panorama, cada vez más personas han empezado a adquirir criptomonedas para poder invertir en algo "seguro" y "fiable" tanto a corto como a largo plazo, a pesar de los niveles extremos de inestabilidad que sufre constantemente.
Sin embargo, invertir o comprar en criptodivisas es más fácil de lo que parece. Hay que recordar que se trata de monedas virtuales, por lo que serán controladas en carteras o monederos que comparten esa particularidad, pues a diferencia del dinero corriente, no tienen un soporte físico.
El precio de las criptomonedas hoy
Esta es la cotización de las criptodivisas más destacadas en este momento.
El Bitcoin, cotiza a 59.663,39 dólares, lo que implicó un cambio de -0,717% en las últimas horas.
La segunda criptomoneda más popular del mercado, Ethereum, ha mostrado un movimiento de 0,006% en las últimas 24 horas, por lo que su valor se ubica en 1.682,3 dólares.
En el caso de TetherUs, su precio es de 1 dólares, por lo que en el último día tuvo un movimiento de 0,05%.
Por su parte, BNB, tiene un valor de 545,03 dólares, con un cambio de 1,12%, en cambio el Litecoin cotizó a 39.318 dólares, tras una variación de -3.0660923.
Finalmente, el Dogecoin, una de las monedas virtuales que fue impulsada por Elon Musk, tiene un valor de 0,05 dólares tras presentar un cambio de 0,84% en las últimas 24 horas.
Qué pasa con las criptodivisas
Luego de que en las primeras semanas de mayo del 2022 se viviera el "criptocrash" o "criptoinvierno" que dejaron al descubierto la enorme volatilidad de estas monedas digitales, ha llegado un nuevo periodo de relativa estabilidad.
Bitcoin, ethereum y BNB han mostrado variaciones "controladas", puesto que no se han disparado los precios como en semanas previas. Por ejemplo, a inicios de agosto, las mencionadas anteriormente tuvieron un cambio menor del 2%.
Por otra parte, algo que esta llamando la atención en el mundo de las criptomonedas es que China está ablandando sus restricciones y podría comenzar a permitir su uso. Específicamente sería Hong Kong en donde este cambio se haría presente.
Sumado a ello, la plataforma de transacciones digitales PayPal anunció su propia stablecoin llamada PayPal USD (PYUSD), que cuenta por el respaldo de depósitos en dólares, bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos a corto plazo y activos equivalentes.
La compañía ha afirmado en su declaración que permitirá la transferencia de fondos a monederos digitales de terceros y proporcionará detalles sobre cómo integrar su servicio en exchanges centralizados y descentralizados, con el objetivo de ser utilizado en Finanzas Descentralizadas (DeFi, por sus siglas en inglés). Por lo tanto, es muy probable que se utilice ampliamente en la industria Web3.
Su avance en Latinoamérica
Criptomonedas en México: el Banco de México (Banxico) ha determinado que ninguna de las instituciones que participan en el sistema financiero nacional podrá hacer uso o deberá permitir operaciones de ninguna clase a través de este medio de pago.
En territorio mexicano el empresario Ricardo Salinas Pliego, uno de los más ricos del país, ha mostrado interés en las criptomonedas y ha asegurado que varios de sus negocios aceptarán bitcoin en el futuro, incluido su banco; hasta el momento una de sus tiendas más populares ya lo hace.
Criptomonedas en Perú: el Banco Central de Reserva del Perú (BCR) ha dejado en claro que su misión no es ser el primero ni el segundo banco central que regule el uso de las criptomonedas, ello debido a la inestabilidad que las caracteriza. Sin embargo, hace días el presidente del (BCR) aseguró que el BCR trabajaba en un proyecto de moneda digital propia.
Criptomonedas en Colombia: en la nación sudamericana hay más de 500 sitios donde es permitido pagar con criptodivisas. Colombia ocupa el puesto 14 entre 26 países de adopción de criptomonedas, según el informe de Finder.
Criptomonedas en Centroamérica: en el gobierno de El Salvador, el bitcoin, que en septiembre de 2021 se convirtió en moneda de curso legal, ha perdido oficialmente este estatus en este enero del 2025 tras una reforma aprobada por la Asamblea Legislativa del país. Según informó la prensa local, la modificación de la Ley Bitcoin fue impulsada por el gobierno del presidente Nayib Bukele y respaldada por la mayoría oficialista en el órgano legislativo. Este cambio marca el fin de una política que había colocado al país centroamericano en el centro del debate global sobre las criptomonedas.
¿Cómo crear una criptomoneda?
Al momento de crear una criptomoneda es importante primero determinar qué se desea tener: una moneda o un token. La primera usa su propia blockchain, mientras que la segunda se basa en una red preexistente.
De acuerdo con el sitio de Binance, para crear una criptomoneda se necesita de un gran equipo de desarrolladores y expertos; mientras que para el token sí se requieren conocimientos técnicos pero es posible crearlo en minutos a través del uso de otras blockchains como Ethereum o BNB, que son las más populares.
Los costos de creación, el tiempo requerido y el uso de fuerza de trabajo dependerá de si se opta por hacer una moneda virtual o un token. En éste último caso también se puede usar un código establecido para crear tokens o pagar para usar un servicio de creación de monedas.
Es importante saber que antes de crear una criptomoneda se debe considerar su utilidad y estado legal.
En el caso de elegir crear una criptomoneda, entonces se debe elegir una blockchain, posteriormente se debe hacer un plan acorde al funcionamiento y la funcionalidad de la blockchain para diseñar los nodos y la interfaz.

articles.title: Cette montre connectée Garmin notée 5/5 tombe à 530 € à l'occasion du Black Friday 2026
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 : La montre connectée Garmin Fenix 8 "5 étoiles" à 530,00 €
À l'occasion du Black Friday, la Garmin Fenix 8 passe à 530,00 € chez Amazon, soit une baisse d'environ 7 % et 38,73 € d'économie. Dotée d'un écran Amoled lumineux ainsi que de capteurs GPS et cardio très précis pour les activités outdoor, cette montre connectée affiche actuellement la note de 5/5 dans nos tests.
La montre connectée Garmin Fenix 8 cible les sportifs exigeants et les adeptes d'activités de plein air avec une montée en gamme marquée par l'arrivée d'un écran Amoled, d'un micro et d'un profondimètre. Ce modèle multisport s'est distingué lors de son passage dans notre labo en associant des matériaux résistants à des fonctions du quotidien.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, la Garmin Fenix 8 descend à 530,00 € chez Amazon, soit environ 7 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours (568,73 €). Cette baisse de prix permet d'économiser 38,73 €.
Garmin Fenix 8 : un équipement complet pour le sport et le quotidien
La Garmin Fenix 8 affiche actuellement la note de 5/5 dans nos colonnes. Notre rédaction a salué la précision du suivi cardiaque et du positionnement par satellite lors de notre test complet. Le passage à une dalle Amoled apporte un affichage plus lumineux et détaillé que les écrans transflectifs précédents, tout en conservant une réactivité tactile sans accroc pour consulter ses données d'entraînement.
Le boîtier intègre désormais un micro et un haut-parleur pour gérer les appels ou les commandes vocales directement depuis le poignet. Les amateurs de plongée profitent également d'une étanchéité certifiée jusqu'à 100 m et d'un profondimètre intégré pour suivre leurs immersions.
Garmin Fenix 8
Points forts
- Dalle Amoled plus lumineuse et offrant plus d’informations que les écrans MIP transflectifs.
- Matériaux solides et belles finitions.
- Micro et haut-parleur.
- Lampe torche.
- Autonomie correcte pour un écran Amoled.
- Précision du GPS et du cardiofréquencemètre.
- Très bonne réactivité de l’écran tactile.
Points faibles
- Montre lourde au cadran épais.
- Interface repensée, mais toujours aussi dense (plusieurs jours sont nécessaires pour s’y habituer).
- L’app ne change pas, mais pourrait être plus intuitive.
- Utilisateurs iOS toujours plus lésés que les utilisateurs Android.
Robustesse maximale et interface complète pour l'outdoor
Construite avec des matériaux solides, cette montre multisport dispose d'une lampe torche intégrée très pratique pour courir de nuit ou s'orienter dans l'obscurité. Sa mémoire interne de 32 Go autorise le stockage de titres musicaux pour s'entraîner sans emporter son smartphone, tandis que la batterie assure une autonomie adaptée aux sorties prolongées malgré les exigences de l'écran lumineux.
Le boîtier volumineux se fait ressentir sur les petits poignets et l'interface Garmin demande plusieurs jours de prise en main en raison de la profusion d'options, mais ces détails ne gêneront pas les sportifs réguliers en quête d'un suivi très complet.
Garmin Forerunner 970 : l'autre option face au Garmin Fenix 8
Également notée 5/5 à ce jour par nos testeurs, la Garmin Forerunner 970 partage de nombreuses fonctions sportives de pointe dans un format orienté vers la course à pied. Elle se distingue par une ergonomie générale axée sur la légèreté lors des entraînements sur piste ou sur route.
Face à la Garmin Forerunner 970, la Garmin Fenix 8 conserve l'avantage de ses matériaux renforcés et de son profondimètre dédié aux sports nautiques, avec un tarif inférieur de 69,00 € grâce à la promotion actuelle.
Garmin Forerunner 970
Points forts
- Finitions haut de gamme.
- Écran Oled de qualité.
- Garmin Pay.
- Garmin Connect.
- GNSS double bande précis.
- Lampe torche.
- 13 jours d'autonomie.
Points faibles
- Capteur cardio parfois faillible sur les variations d'intensité.
