articles.title: Europe's biggest AI challenge isn't the technology. It's organizational psychology
articles.text:
Europe's biggest AI challenge isn't the technology. It's organizational psychology
Why Europe’s AI ambitions depend on understanding employees
Despite years of discussions and pilot projects, only 25% of EU workers use artificial intelligence (AI) for work purposes, compared to 43% of employees in the US. The gap is not simply about access to better tools or frontier models but reflects how organizations manage change.
President EMEA at Cognizant.
Too many European organizations make the same fundamental mistake, conflating access to AI with its adoption. Often, this comes across as broad mandates to employees, asking them to be more productive through AI but then leaving them to figure out what that means for their role. Our own research has found that over a third of employees are still looking for clear reasons to adopt AI.
If Europe wants to persuade its workforce that AI is an enabler rather than a threat, then it needs to rethink how it builds confidence, trust and motivation across the workforce.
Understand workers’ concerns
Every employee approaches work, risk and technology in unique ways. Their fears and concerns vary depending on stage of career, level of tech skill and more.
Despite these differences, 41% of workers in the EU are at least somewhat concerned about job displacement due to AI, with some of the highest fear appearing among younger individuals preparing to enter the job market.
Meanwhile, current workers are split on attitudes towards the technology. Our research found over 60 different personas, grouped into seven broad archetypes. Some readily adopt AI tools, while others are more cautious or need more persuading. There are also workers who are simply unsure where to begin their journey or how it fits into their working life.
Age and career stage also shape these attitudes. As Europe’s workforce grows older, some experienced employees may worry about becoming obsolete or question the value of learning entirely new ways of working late in their careers. This makes it harder to change long-established working habits.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Finally, even when workers do want to use AI, 82% report they are regularly unsatisfied with the tools they are actually given. This can quickly lead to them being put off further adoption due to these bad experiences and slow future roll-outs further.
Without intentional support, no matter how many tools businesses buy, they will still fail to see a return on investment.
Get the workforce onside
Leaders need to understand workers’ anxiety is not unfounded. Cognizant predicted in 2023 that by 2032, 90% of jobs would be disrupted by AI. But more recent research found that that target was reached six years ahead of schedule.
Leaders can’t gloss over that, and if they want to bridge the gap between employees and AI initiatives, they need to start building trust, which starts with honesty. Executives should be clear about what has been decided, what remains uncertain and where automation is still being tested. This gives employees the information needed to understand where they fit, how their role could change and what support will be available.
This must also be supported by reskilling, support and development pathways to ensure enterprises are preparing their workforces for these new ways of working. This doesn’t mean a complete change to a person’s career but instead ensuring they have the skills necessary to combine AI capabilities with their existing domain expertise.
The conversation around AI also needs to be reframed. Rather than focusing on automation, leaders should prioritize improving effectiveness, expanding capabilities and elevating the quality and impact of human work.
Build for behavior, not technology
Businesses need to change how they approach transformation. Principally, this means moving from individual tech projects to business wide change across all teams. The first step of this process is leadership teams adapting their mindset from AI being the solution to their problems to building for outcomes which are enabled by AI.
This can be done in three simple steps:
Define an intention architecture. Instead of focusing the program on what the technology can do, successful organizations anchor it in what they want people to do differently. They design from desired behavioral outcomes backward, clarifying the human actions, decisions and workflows AI should change.
Normalize experimentation. Most teams don’t feel psychologically safe enough to try, fail and iterate in the open. High‑performing organizations create structured spaces where experimentation is expected, supported and de‑risked. This makes learning part of the job, not a side project.
Model the behavior through managers and influencers. People adopt what they see, not what they’re told. When managers and respected peers actively use AI tools in their day‑to‑day work, the shift becomes cultural rather than policy‑driven.
Shifting the mindset for the future
Europe will not close its AI adoption gap simply by giving more employees access to more powerful tools. It will close it when organizations give people a clear reason to use AI, the confidence to experiment and an honest account of how work will change. The technology is ready. The determining factor will be whether leaders can bring their workforce with them.

articles.title: Neuralink trial participant ditches mouth stick to play GTA 6 with his mind — brain-computer interface maps imagined ring-finger taps and hand slides to a PlayStation 5 controller
articles.text:
Neuralink trial participant ditches mouth stick to play GTA 6 with his mind — brain-computer interface maps imagined ring-finger taps and hand slides to a PlayStation 5 controller
‘You immediately get your portal to the world back.’
Elon Musk’s Neuralink started clinical trials less than three years ago, and patients are seeing impressive results. The latest demonstration of this brain computer interface comes via a video on social media showing an unnamed medical trial participant playing GTA 6. According to the video, the team behind the implant mapped different i,agined movements to a PlayStation 5 controller, allowing the player to simulate controller actions using his thoughts. For example, thinking about tapping their ring finger activated the square button while imagining sliding their right hand forward pulled the nose of the airplane up. They also mentioned another control being bound to their foot, it’s unclear what action this allowed.
The first Neuralink device was implanted in January 2024, with the patient able to move a mouse just by thinking. Once they’ve been able to master the basics of using a computer, like moving a mouse and using the keyboard, through the brain-computer interface (BCI), one of the next steps that some patients take is to play a game on their system. Just a couple of months after the first implant, we’ve already seen reports of people using Neuralink to play turn-based games like chess and Civilization VI. By August 2024, the second Neuralink recipient was reportedly playing Counter-Strike 2, with the patient calling the experience “insane.”
Before Neuralink "I was essentially like a bird just pecking at an iPad."
Today, we already have people playing complicated games like World of Warcraft and GTA VI using BCI implants. This is an achievement for Neuralink and a life-changing capability for patients who have lost mobility. The patient who streamed their GTA VI gameplay said that they’ve previously used a mouth stick, but it was miles away from the Neuralink chip they have in their head. “Before the … chip and surgery, I was using a mouth stick and an iPad. I was essentially like a bird just pecking at an iPad. There was (sic) like a few games I could play, but like obviously it made your jaw sore, it made everything sore,” the patient said. “So, then I get a chip, and I was like what does this let me do. Immediately, controlling a computer is like boom, ‘portal to the world,’ like you just immediately get your portal to the world back.”
Aside from giving people the ability to control computing devices with their mind, Neuralink is also working on a technology, called Blindsight, that will restore sight to blind people. Musk claims that it’s already “ready from an engineering standpoint,” and that the company is only waiting for regulatory approval before it can begin human testing.

articles.title: Ein Kabel für alles? Worauf es beim Docking ankommt
articles.text:
USB-C ist nicht gleich USB-C: Worauf es beim Setup für Büro und unterwegs ankommt
Im Homeoffice steht ein Schreibtisch bereit, im Büro nutzt du vielleicht einen geteilten Platz. Vor einer Präsentation außer Haus prüfst du, welche Ausstattung dich dort erwartet und was du mitbringen musst.
Bild und Strom über ein Kabel
Ein Kabel kann das Notebook mit Bildschirm, Tastatur, Maus und Netzwerk verbinden und zugleich laden. Notebook, Monitor oder Dock und Kabel müssen dafür die gewünschten Funktionen unterstützen. Prüfe diese drei Punkte:
- Bild: Der USB-C-Anschluss des Notebooks muss Bildsignale ausgeben können. In den technischen Daten wird diese Funktion meist als DisplayPort Alt Mode bezeichnet.
- Strom: Über den Standard USB Power Delivery (USB PD) handeln Notebook und Stromquelle die Ladeleistung aus. Entscheidend ist, was am Notebook ankommt. Liefert das Dock 65 Watt und braucht das Notebook unter Last mehr, kann sich der Akku trotz Anschluss entladen.
- Mehrere Monitore: Prüfe, welche Anzahl, Auflösung und Bildwiederholrate Notebook und Dock gemeinsam unterstützen.
Ein Monitor mit integrierter Dockingfunktion kann das Notebook laden und mit USB-Zubehör verbinden. Je nach Modell kommt ein Netzwerkanschluss hinzu. Reichen seine Funktionen aus, brauchst du kein separates Dock. Vorhandene Bildschirme ohne integrierte Dockingfunktion kannst du über eine separate Dockingstation mit dem Notebook verbinden.
Beispiele für beide Anschlusswege:
- Lenovo ThinkVision P27QD-40: 27-Zoll-Monitor mit 2.560 × 1.440 Pixeln, USB-C-Docking, USB-Hub und Netzwerkanschluss; bis zu 140 Watt Power Delivery für kompatible Notebooks.
- ThinkPad USB4 Dock 5000: verbindet Bildschirme, USB-Zubehör und Netzwerk mit dem Notebook; mit dem mitgelieferten Netzteil bis zu 65 Watt Ladeleistung.
Bildfläche und Eingabe am festen Platz
Die Bildfläche richtet sich nach deinen Aufgaben. Auf einem Ultrawide-Monitor im breiten 21:9-Format passen etwa Tabelle und Präsentation nebeneinander. Für eine einzelne Anwendung kann ein 27-Zoll-Bildschirm genügen. Auflösung und Textskalierung sollten gut lesbare Schrift ermöglichen.
Auch ein Ultrawide-Monitor kann integriertes Docking mitbringen. Separate Tastatur und Maus lassen sich unabhängig vom Notebook platzieren. Ein umschaltbares Tastatur-Maus-Set wechselt zwischen mehreren verbundenen Rechnern. Für Bildfläche und Eingabe am festen Platz:
- Lenovo ThinkVision P34WD-40: Höhenverstellbarer und neigbarer 34-Zoll-Curved-Ultrawide-Monitor mit 3.440 × 1.440 Pixeln und USB-C-Docking. Über den integrierten KVM-Umschalter lassen sich ein Notebook und ein stationärer PC mit derselben Tastatur und Maus bedienen.
- Lenovo Wireless Multi-Mode Pro Combo Keyboard and Mouse 6000: Kabelloses Set aus Tastatur und Maus, umschaltbar zwischen bis zu drei verbundenen Geräten.
Unterwegs das Richtige einpacken
Wenn du auswärts präsentierst, kläre vorab die Anschlüsse von Bildschirm oder Beamer. Kennst du die Ausstattung am Ziel nicht, packe dein Notebook-Netzteil ein. Eine Maus mit Präsentationsmodus kann als Fernbedienung dienen: Tasten blättern durch die Folien, ein digitaler Zeiger hebt Inhalte hervor.
Ein faltbares Headset eignet sich für Videocalls am Schreibtisch und unterwegs. Aktive Geräuschunterdrückung (ANC) reduziert Umgebungsgeräusche beim Zuhören. Wie gut andere deine Stimme verstehen, hängt von den Mikrofonen und ihrer Signalverarbeitung ab.
Ein Steckerladegerät mit zwei USB-C-Buchsen versorgt Notebook und Smartphone über je ein Kabel an der Steckdose. Das Dock am Schreibtisch verbindet zusätzlich Bildschirme, Zubehör und Netzwerk.
Beispiele für Präsentationen, Videocalls und das Laden unterwegs:
- ThinkPad Bluetooth Presenter Mouse (Aura Edition): Wechselt durch Drehen zwischen Maus- und Präsentationsmodus, mit Tasten zur Foliensteuerung und digitalem Zeiger.
- ThinkPad Dual-Mode Wireless ANC Foldable Headset 8550 (Aura Edition): Faltbares, für Microsoft Teams zertifiziertes Headset mit adaptiver Geräuschunterdrückung, nativem Bluetooth und USB-C-Bluetooth-Empfänger
- Lenovo Dual USB-C 65W GaN Charger: Kompaktes GaN-Ladegerät mit zwei USB-C-Anschlüssen; bei gleichzeitiger Nutzung werden bis zu 45 W und 18 W auf die beiden Anschlüsse verteilt
Checkliste für den nächsten Ortswechsel
- Unterstützt dein Notebook die benötigten Bildschirme und ihre Auflösung?
- Reicht die verfügbare Ladeleistung für dein Notebook?
- Kennst du die Ausstattung am Ziel und hast du das fehlende Zubehör eingepackt?

articles.title: Hace 2.000 años, en Menorca despedían a sus muertos por todo lo alto: con vino y leche
articles.text:
En Alaior, un pequeño pueblo situado en la costa sur de Menorca, además de unas playas espectaculares hay una necrópolis de cuevas artificiales excavadas en la roca en Cales Coves. Pues bien, ese yacimiento acaba de dejarnos un descubrimiento de lo más llamativo sobre cómo eran los funerales hace 2.000 años. En una frase: se lo montaban a lo grande.
El hallazgo. Delante de la cueva 45 hay un patio abierto que, como cuenta la arqueóloga Sònia Carbonell al diari Ara, se creó expresamente para realizar rituales de despedida. Quienes acudieron a esos funerales dejaron unas vasijas cuyo contenido no se había identificado hasta ahora.
Un equipo de la UAB, el Barcelona Supercomputing Center y la Universitat Pompeu Fabra ha analizado los residuos orgánicos de 34 vasijas de cerámica de esa cueva y ha descubierto que los pequeños contenían principalmente lácteos, además de trazas de vino en otras vasijas que tenían formas inspiradas en el Mediterráneo, sobre todo en el mundo púnico. Una de las piezas con pico vertedor, de la que se pensaba inicialmente que era una aceitera, tenía una mezcla de lácteos con fruta y se cree que probablemente hiciera las veces de biberón.
Por qué importa. Porque es la primera vez en la isla que se documenta el uso del vino en un ritual funerario menorquín. Hay que tener en cuenta que por aquel entonces el vino era un producto de fuera, de uso más ocasional. La leche, por el contrario, era un producto básico y cotidiano (concretamente, la de cabra y oveja).
Los menorquines de la época copiaron recipientes extranjeros, pero los usaron a su manera. Como sintetiza Carbonell, la comunidad integraba productos y formas de fuera manteniendo sus códigos culturales y su identidad. Que hubiera un biberón sugiere que en ese momento de la despedida también se quería recordar el cuidado de los niños.
Cómo lo descubrieron. Estas piezas se recuperaron entre 2023 y 2024 y muchas de ellas no solo estaban intactas, sino que seguían en su posición original. Después, escanearon los objetos, los microexcavaron y los analizaron químicamente. Además de lácteos y vino, identificaron grasas animales y aceites vegetales varios.
Los completos y complejos funerales menorquines. Dentro de la lista de Patrimonio Mundial de la UNESCO están los restos de la cultura talayótica de Menorca, que tenía unos rituales funerarios bastante complejos, como teñir de rojo el pelo de quienes fallecían o cortarles un mechón. Después, en el periodo posttalayótico, los contactos con el exterior aumentaron. Sin ir más lejos, Carbonell señalaba en una investigación anterior que la arquitectura funeraria sugería que hubo interacción con grupos púnicos.
Vaya por delante algo: este tipo de recipientes ya eran conocidos. De hecho, el Museu de Menorca estudió 269 vasos altos pertenecientes al al hipogeo de Sa Mola y los relacionó con una práctica funeraria de ofrendas y de banquetes La primera campaña de excavación en Cales Coves ya indicaba prácticas rituales entre los siglos IV-III y I a. C. Ahora sabemos que el patio y el interior de la cueva tenían funciones distintas: el biberón acompañaba al difunto dentro de la cámara a modo de ofrenda, mientras que en el patio tenía lugar el banquete, como evidencian los restos de cabras, ovejas y cerdos.

articles.title: AI is doing to programmers what it did to farmers, weavers: Sridhar Vembu
articles.text:
AI is doing to programmers what it did to farmers, weavers: Sridhar Vembu
Sridhar Vembu argues AI could transform intellectual work just as mechanisation transformed traditional trades, citing examples of AI tackling complex coding and engineering tasks with striking speed.
What mechanisation and automation did to farmers, weavers, carpenters and ironsmiths could now be happening to mathematicians and programmers, according to Zoho co-founder Sridhar Vembu.
He believes artificial intelligence (AI) is beginning to displace work traditionally associated with highly skilled intellectual professionals, just as earlier technological advances transformed occupations built around manual skills and craftsmanship.
In a post on X, Vembu backed an observation by AI researcher Subbarao Kambhampati that the intellectual class had largely been spared the loss of purpose experienced by workers displaced by previous technological revolutions. He illustrated the shift with two examples from his own experience.
Vembu said he asked AI to optimise code while travelling, a task he estimated would take a very capable programmer at least a month. “AI understood my high level intent very clearly and came up with a detailed plan and cleanly executed it and tested it against very detailed and exhaustive test cases it had constructed itself. The whole thing cost about $4 in tokens,” he wrote.
His second example is a colleague with no engineering background who used a personal AI account to create a mechanical CAD design for a motor housing. Vembu said the AI operated newly released, low-cost CAD software installed on the colleague’s computer, adding that he doubted the tool had been part of the model’s training. The point, in his telling, is that AI can help people attempt technical work previously beyond their reach.
Vembu quoted AI researcher Subbarao Kambhampati’s observation that “The intellectual class never quite experienced the loss of purpose in their lives that many other classes of humans experienced.”
Kambhampati argues that earlier mechanisation displaced weavers and craftspeople, but AI now threatens mathematicians, programmers and other knowledge workers. The anxiety, he suggests, reflects a newly affected class mistaking a loss of individual purpose for a crisis of humanity. Future generations may adapt to AI doing much of today’s intellectual work.
The tools are moving in that direction. Anthropic’s analysis of about 400,000 Claude Code sessions found that users typically made planning decisions while AI handled much of the execution. It also noted that people across occupations completed coding tasks at rates close to software engineers. Microsoft added its MAI Code 2 models to GitHub Copilot on November 17 for tasks such as making changes across several files and complex debugging.
Vembu sees both displacement and democratisation. AI may erode the market value of specialised skills while widening access to technical work.

articles.title: Au revoir Gmail et Apple Mail : le client mail français Open Mailbox débarque sur iOS et Android
articles.text:
Dans la galaxie des clients de messagerie sur mobile, il y a généralement trois écoles : ceux qui utilisent l’application Gmail, ceux qui utilisent Outlook, et ceux qui configurent l’appli Apple Mail sur leur iPhone. Des choix qui sont souvent guidés par le fait que les fournisseurs d’e-mails proposent leur propre application, comme c’est le cas pour Gmail et Outlook. Et pour cause, ces applications proposent une intégration parfaite avec les différents outils proposés par les éditeurs. Mais ces clients de messagerie ont tous un point commun : celui d’être développé par des géants de la Tech.
Il existe pourtant pléthore d’alternatives souveraines pour lire vos e-mails sur votre smartphone Android ou votre iPhone. Open Mailbox en fait d’ailleurs partie. Cette application développée en France par l’entreprise toulousaine Soluce Technologies est gratuite, open source, et compatible avec les principaux fournisseurs de messagerie.
Un client de messagerie qui mise sur la confidentialité
Outre son code ouvert et sa gratuité, Open Mailbox met en avant sa philosophie misant sur la confidentialité de vos données. Le client de messagerie, qui ne nécessite aucune inscription ni aucun compte pour être utilisé, communique directement vers les serveurs IMAP et SMTP de vos fournisseurs d’e-mail.
Vos messages ne transitent par aucun serveur intermédiaire et aucune copie de vos messages n’est conservée nulle part. Vos identifiants restent par ailleurs stockés dans l’espace sécurisé propre à votre smartphone.
Par ailleurs, l’application n’embarque aucun traqueur, aucune publicité et aucun outil de télémétrie visant à analyser vos habitudes d’utilisation. Open Mailbox bloque d’ailleurs par défaut toutes les images distantes dans les emails entrants pour éviter le pistage.
Quid du modèle économique ? L’éditeur explique en réponse à un commentaire d’un redditeur que son « modèle économique repose sur le développement de logiciels, leur intégration et la fourniture de services managés aux entreprises, notamment autour de solutions open source comme Nextcloud ».
« Ces activités commerciales financent notre entreprise et nous permettent de développer et de maintenir des applications open source pour la communauté, notamment Open Mailbox. Nous ne dépendons donc ni des dons ni des abonnements à nos applications pour assurer le fonctionnement de notre entreprise. » complète l’entreprise toulousaine Soluce Technologies.
Un client mail complet mais avec quelques limitations
Comme la plupart des clients de messagerie, Open Mailbox propose une boîte de réception unifiée regroupant toutes les messageries que vous configurez. Open Mailbox trie vos messages localement sur votre smartphone en organisant ceux-ci par catégories.
Le client de messagerie privilégie également le fonctionnement hors ligne. Ainsi, tous les emails sont conservés localement sur votre appareil. La recherche textuelle intégrée fonctionne également entièrement hors ligne avec la mise en surbrillance des termes recherchés.
Comme dans la plupart des clients de messagerie, Open Mailbox permet d’annuler une action (comme l’archivage ou la suppression accidentelle d’un message) pendant 5 secondes. L’application vous permettra également de vous désinscrire facilement des listes de diffusion en un clic.
L’application est compatible avec Gmail, iCloud, OVHCloud, IONOS, Yahoo ainsi que tous les serveurs IMAP / SMTP standard. À noter toutefois que la configuration de vos comptes de messagerie se fait manuellement et ne passe pas par une connexion via l’interface de votre fournisseur. Pour les utilisateurs de Gmail, par exemple, il sera indispensable de créer au préalable un « mot de passe d’application » dans votre compte Google pour pouvoir connecter votre messagerie dans l’application.
Par ailleurs, Open Mailbox ne prend pour l’instant pas en charge les messageries de Microsoft (Outlook, hotmail, etc.), celles-ci utilisant le protocole d’authentification Oauth qui n’est pour l’heure pas encore pris en charge par Open Mailbox. L’éditeur précise néanmoins que la prise en charge de ces comptes est prévue et en cours de développement dans l’application.

articles.title: Italia multó a Meta con 805 millones de euros por acceder a las fotos de Facebook en teléfonos Android
articles.text:
La autoridad de protección de datos de Italia, el Garante, multó a Meta con 805 millones de euros por acceder a las fotos y los videos de usuarios de Facebook en teléfonos Android sin un consentimiento específico. La empresa tecnológica anunció que apelará.
El organismo concluyó que la aplicación pidió un único permiso del sistema para acceder a fotos y videos, válido para varias funciones, y que lo hizo con un aviso genérico. Ese permiso no bastó, según el regulador, para autorizar la función bajo examen: las sugerencias de publicación tomadas de la galería del teléfono.
La función se llama “Ottieni suggerimenti dalla galleria quando navighi su Facebook” (en español, recibir sugerencias de la galería mientras se navega por Facebook). Muestra fotos y videos guardados en el dispositivo como ideas para compartir en la red social. Según el Garante, está disponible desde 2023 y venía activada por defecto.
El Garante calculó que unos 20 millones de usuarios de Android en Italia podían estar afectados. La multa equivale a cerca del 0,47% de la facturación mundial del grupo, informó el organismo en su comunicado del 14 de noviembre.
Un permiso general para varias funciones
La resolución explica que, antes de la autorización, la app mostraba una pantalla según la cual el acceso servía para “compartir fotos y videos, recibir sugerencias sobre las fotos que se suben y habilitar otras funciones”. Para el Garante, ese texto no permitía entender que se autorizaba también la función de sugerencias.
Una vez concedido en su modalidad completa, el permiso de Android permite a la app leer todo el archivo multimedia del teléfono, por lo general de forma permanente. El usuario solo puede retirarlo desde los ajustes del dispositivo. El Garante añadió que ni el usuario ni la autoridad pueden comprobar qué información se usa realmente.
La norma aplicada es el artículo 122 del Código de Privacidad italiano, que traslada al derecho del país la directiva europea ePrivacy. Considera el teléfono parte de la esfera privada y exige un consentimiento libre e informado para acceder a lo que guarda, aunque los datos no se transmitan ni haya un daño.
El Garante rechazó además la objeción de Meta, que sostenía que el caso correspondía a la autoridad irlandesa por el mecanismo de ventanilla única del reglamento europeo de datos (GDPR). Según el regulador, la normativa ePrivacy no prevé ese mecanismo.
Qué deberá cambiar Meta y cómo se fijó el monto
Meta tiene 60 días desde la notificación para pedir el consentimiento con una solicitud separada y específica, explicar para qué sirve la función y mantenerla desactivada por defecto, también para quienes ya dieron el permiso. Debe informar de las primeras medidas en 30 días y de su aplicación en 90. Si no se adapta, la función no podrá operar sin consentimiento válido.
Para fijar el monto, el Garante tuvo en cuenta el número de personas implicadas, la duración de la infracción, una resolución de 2019 contra la misma empresa y la escasa colaboración durante la investigación. Consideró atenuantes los cambios que Meta introdujo después de la denuncia, aunque los calificó de tardíos y limitados a quienes actualizan la app.
El caso nació de una denuncia presentada el 10 de julio de 2025 por el Centro de Defensa del Consumidor de Bolzano. La denuncia planteaba un vínculo con el entrenamiento de sistemas de inteligencia artificial de Meta, pero el Garante precisó que no examinó ese punto, que la empresa niega.
Meta apelará y el Garante evaluará otra función
Un portavoz de Meta dijo que la empresa está “en total desacuerdo” con la valoración de los hechos y la aplicación de la norma, y que considera desproporcionado el monto. Según el vocero, se trata de una función simple, el usuario debe conceder un permiso en el dispositivo y puede cambiarlo cuando quiera. Meta afirmó que presentará un recurso.
El Garante se reservó la posibilidad de investigar por separado otra función, lanzada en la Unión Europea a comienzos de 2026, que procesa en la nube el contenido de la galería. La resolución indica que ese punto no formó parte de este procedimiento.

articles.title: OpenAI’s chief scientist has thoughts on how to limit AI development | TechCrunch
articles.text:
A new blog post from OpenAI’s chief scientist Jakub Pachocki discusses potential limits on AI development, with a focus on a measurement called perplexity.
Slowing AI development became a particularly hot topic after a former OpenAI and Anthropic researcher said the companies were “gambling with our lives,” and even Anthropic’s IPO filing suggested that the technology could pose “catastrophic or existential risks to society.”
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei then published a plan to “pace the frontier,” seemingly endorsed by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk. Among other things, Amodei called for companies to agree to “common safety standards as well as limits on the rate of unchecked AI progress.”
But to establish a speed limit on AI development, you need to agree on how you measure speed. Pachocki’s post — described by Altman as “the most important thing OpenAI has published in a while” — suggests perplexity (not to be confused with the company of the same name) could be that measurement.
In Pachochki’s argument, benchmarks that focus on AI’s “downstream capabilities” have quickly become outdated as the technology advances. But perplexity — which “measures how well a model predicts the next token on average; lower perplexity means better predictions” — has remained “informative.”
Pachochki’s post includes a chart of how the perplexity of OpenAI’s models has fallen since GPT 3.5.
“GPT‑4, at ~0.91, was proficient at utilizing chain-of-thought reasoning productively, which motivated the subsequent targeted elicitation of this capability and the creation of modern reasoning models,” he wrote. “Now, as we have reached losses below 0.8, we have seen the emergence of transformative capabilities in fields like cybersecurity and mathematics.”
So in his view, perplexity could provide the basis for “a shared benchmark for general intelligence,” which AI companies could then use to establish “common limits.” With perplexity serving as a standard measurement for AI progress, the companies would commit not to go past a certain threshold “until our ability to understand and monitor AI behavior achieves a certain concrete milestone.”

articles.title: AI is redrawing the line between product and engineering - creating a competitive edge
articles.text:
AI is redrawing the line between product and engineering - creating a competitive edge
AI is driving shared ownership, faster decisions, and stronger outcomes
The division of responsibilities between product and engineering has always been distinct; product teams decided what should be built, engineering teams determined how to build it, and organizations invested heavily in improving the handover between them.
Today, those traditional norms and expectations are changing. As AI accelerates software development, prototyping and decision support, the traditional boundaries between product and engineering are becoming increasingly artificial.
SVP, Global Head of Digital Technology Services at Intellias.
While that’s definitely creating friction as long-established ways of working evolve, it also presents a much bigger opportunity: shifting the conversation from improving individual teams to building capability that compounds across the business.
Product leaders are being drawn into conversations about AI capabilities, data, governance and technical trade-offs. Engineers, meanwhile, are expected to think more deeply about customer outcomes, trust and commercial priorities.
Over the past 12 months, I’ve been surprised to observe how quickly AI has re-drawn the line between product and engineering, and I believe this convergence will become one of AI’s most significant organizational impacts.
There’s a significant competitive advantage to be gained from rethinking how product and engineering make decisions together, rather than simply how they collaborate.
AI has changed where value is created
Much of the conversation around AI has focused on engineering productivity, and that’s completely understandable. The ability to generate code and accelerate delivery can be transformative, but focusing only on speed misses the bigger opportunity.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
As software becomes easier to build, competitive advantage will shift toward making better product decisions and adapting more quickly once software reaches customers. That changes what organizations need from both product and engineering.
Product leaders can no longer rely on customer insight alone. They need enough technical understanding to judge what's genuinely possible, where AI creates value and where its limitations introduce risk.
At the same time, engineers are becoming much more involved in product thinking. AI-powered products don't stop evolving once they're released, so technical teams need to understand how customers use them, where trust breaks down and which changes will improve adoption. As a result, these technical decisions increasingly influence commercial outcomes.
The rise of the product engineer
One of the most interesting organizational shifts emerging from this convergence is the rise of the product engineer. I don't see this as a new job title, as much as a new mindset.
As AI takes on more of the implementation work, the most valuable engineers are those who understand the product as well as the technology. They connect technical decisions with customer needs, commercial priorities and long-term business goals instead of focusing solely on implementation.
That same evolution is happening within product management. AI-assisted prototyping makes it easier to test ideas, explore solutions and validate assumptions before development begins. Product managers are becoming more technically confident, while engineers are developing a much deeper understanding of the product domain.
Neither discipline is replacing the other. Instead, the gap between them is narrowing because AI removes much of the routine work that once separated their responsibilities.
Operating models need to evolve
Technology teams are largely still structured around specialist functions, with work moving sequentially between product, design and engineering; an approach that increasingly creates friction.
AI tools may accelerate development, but every approval cycle, clarification meeting and organizational hand-off still slows delivery. In many cases, those delays now take longer than the implementation itself.
That's why more organizations are experimenting with cross-functional AI Pods. Rather than traditional squads of seven or eight people, these smaller teams bring together product, engineering and business expertise around a shared outcome.
With AI taking on much of the implementation work, the team’s focus shifts towards supervision, judgement and decision-making, allowing them to resolve questions more quickly and move faster together. Most importantly, these teams stay collectively responsible for the customer outcome.
This changes leadership as well. Engineers with stronger product understanding can make more day-to-day decisions independently, reducing unnecessary escalation while giving product leaders more time to focus on strategy, prioritization and customer needs.
This isn't only about speed gains. The biggest benefit is in ownership. When teams understand both the technical challenges and the business objective, they tend to make better decisions throughout the whole product lifecycle instead of waiting for direction at every stage.
AI is changing the nature of technology leadership
AI is reshaping what makes product and engineering organizations valuable. As execution becomes easier to automate, competitive advantage shifts towards judgement, domain expertise and a deep understanding of customer problems.
That requires more than adopting AI tools. It means redesigning operating models around shared ownership, faster decision-making and clearer accountability for outcomes, rather than preserving organizational boundaries that were designed for a different era of software development.
As AI becomes embedded across the software lifecycle, the distinction between product and engineering will continue to narrow. Technical fluency and product judgement are becoming complementary capabilities, enabling faster decisions and a clearer focus on delivering customer value.

articles.title: Heiliger Gral der Mathematik: Anthropic-Mitarbeiter will mit Claude die Riemannsche Vermutung bewiesen haben
articles.text:
Heiliger Gral der Mathematik: Anthropic-Mitarbeiter will mit Claude die Riemannsche Vermutung bewiesen haben
SMathematiker und Mathematikerinnen in aller Welt sind in heller Aufruhr, weil das wahrscheinlich berühmteste Problem der Mathematik gelöst worden sein könnte. Ein Mitarbeiter des US-Unternehmens Anthropic behauptet, mit Hilfe der firmeneigenen Künstlichen Intelligenz Claude die sogenannte Riemannsche Vermutung bewiesen zu haben.
Diese Vermutung wird oft auch als „Heiliger Gral“ der Mathematik bezeichnet. „Die Auswirkungen erstrecken sich auf die gesamte Mathematik“, sagte Ghaith Hiary, Mathematiker an der Ohio State University, dem Magazin Science. „Ich hätte nie gedacht, dass ich diesen Tag noch erleben würde … aber nun ist es so weit.“
Schon mehr als 150 Jahre alt
Die Vermutung stammt von dem deutschen Mathematiker Bernhard Riemann, der sie bereits im Jahr 1859 formulierte. Aus seiner Hypothese folgt, dass die Verteilung der Primzahlen – also der natürlichen Zahlen, die nur durch sich selbst und durch 1 teilbar sind – nicht zufällig ist, sondern durch ein tieferes mathematisches Muster bestimmt wird. Die Vermutung hat außerdem weitreichende Konsequenzen in der Zahlentheorie.
Die Riemannsche Vermutung gehört zu den sieben Millenium-Problemen der Mathematik. Für die Lösung hat das US-amerikanische Clay Mathematics Institut im Jahr 2000 je eine Million US-Dollar als Preisgeld ausgelobt.
Bis vor Kurzem war nur eines dieser Millenium-Probleme gelöst. Dann erklärte OpenAI, ein Anthropic-Konkurrent, im September, dass seine KI für eines der Probleme eine Lösung gefunden habe: das Navier-Stokes-Problem, bei dem es um Gleichungen geht, die beschreiben, wie sich Flüssigkeiten bewegen. Offiziell anerkannt ist das noch nicht. Wenige Monate darauf folgt nun möglicherweise die nächste Lösung – durch Levent Alpöge, der auch bei der Navier-Stokes-Veröffentlichung und anderen Mathematik-Lösungen mit Hilfe von KI schon eine Rolle spielte.
KI-Mathematiker staunt über KI
Alpöge erklärt in einem Statement auf seiner Webseite, dass er sich schon seit seiner Zeit als Mathematik-Student mit diesem Problem beschäftigt habe. Er habe die KI-Software Claude auf den Weg gebracht, indem er zwei recht unterschiedliche Ideen kombinierte. „Claude und ich hatten in den letzten Monaten viel Spaß miteinander bei dieser breitgefächerten Arbeit, aber dieses Mal hat Claude mich kurz vor der Ziellinie weit überholt. Nein, Claude flog, tanzte und strahlte kurz vor dieser Ziellinie.“
Die Beweisführung der KI sei unglaublich lang, schreibt Alpöge, in für Menschen verständlicher Sprache sogar mehr als 250.000 Seiten lang, und er fügt hinzu, dass er sie noch nicht in Gänze verstehe. „Ich beabsichtige, mein Bestes zu geben, um diese Beweisführung und ihre bestimmten Vereinfachungen zu verstehen und anderen verständlich zu machen.“
Ayush Khaitan, der beim US-Forschungszentrum Princeton Language and Intelligence im Bereich Mathematik und KI arbeitet, wertet das Ergebnis von Alpöge und Claude als Beweise dafür, dass für solche bahnbrechenden Ergebnisse weiterhin ein Mensch nötig sei. „Es ist klar, dass Alpöge für die Lösung der verallgemeinerten Riemannschen Hypothese ebenso viel Anerkennung verdient wie Claude“, schreibt er auf der Plattform X.
Erste Erklärung: Beweis ist korrekt
Unmittelbar nach der Bekanntgabe beugten sich auch zahlreiche andere Fachleute über den veröffentlichten Computer-Code – bizarrerweise mithilfe von KI, die nötig ist, um die Dokumente zu verstehen. Alpöge veröffentlichte den Beweis bisher als sogenannnten Lean-Code. Die Lean- und Mathlib-Gemeinschaften, ein weltweites Netzwerk aus Mathematikern, Informatikern und Entwicklern, erklärten einen Tag nach der Veröffentlichung: Sie seien «fest davon überzeugt», dass der Beweis korrekt sei.
Die Arbeit von Alpöge und Claude könne völlig neue Forschungsgebiete eröffnen, erklärt der Mathematiker Carlo Pagano, Professor an der Concordia-Universität in Quebec und Gastforscher bei Google DeepMind, gegenüber dem US-amerikanischen Wissenschaftsmagazin Scientific American. „Wenn das zutrifft, erscheint es mir schon bei einer ersten oberflächlichen Durchsicht der Zusammenfassung der vorgeschlagenen Argumentation sehr plausibel, dass die neuen Ideen in dem Beweis völlig neue Denkansätze in der Zahlentheorie eröffnen und neben dem offensichtlich äußerst einflussreichen Ergebnis an sich selbst noch immense Auswirkungen haben werden.“
Auch ein Mensch will die Hypothese gelöst haben
Als wäre die Aufregung in der Mathe-Welt nicht schon groß genug, behaupten nun auch noch zwei weitere Mathematiker, einen rein auf menschlicher Denkarbeit beruhenden Lösungsentwurf für die Riemannsche Vermutung gefunden zu haben, wie unter anderem Science und Scientific American berichten. Alessandro Masullo, ein unabhängiger Mathematiker aus Rom, hat demnach fast zwölf Jahre daran gearbeitet und den Beweis aus Angst vor einer Vorabveröffentlichung unter Verschluss gehalten.
Den Berichten zufolge gab er seinen Entwurf Brian Conrad von der Stanford University, der den Beweis seit Monaten prüfte. Der Plan war, ein weiteres Jahr damit zu verbringen, verbleibende Fehler in dem 940-seitigen Manuskript zu beheben und es zur Begutachtung an Experten weiterzuleiten. Doch die KI-Veröffentlichung bewegte die beiden, das Manuskript herauszugeben. Ob dieses Manuskript der Überprüfung standhält, ist laut dem Artikel noch offen.

articles.title: KFC offers disc-shaped fried chicken to sad disc-less GTA VI fans — KFC Spain’s ‘The Replacement Disc’ campaign delivers where Rockstar disappoints after selling $3.79 billion of GTA VI without a physical disc
articles.text:
KFC offers disc-shaped fried chicken to sad disc-less GTA VI fans — KFC Spain’s ‘The Replacement Disc’ campaign delivers where Rockstar disappoints after selling $3.79 billion of GTA VI without a physical disc
Who could say no to a free piece of suspiciously torus-shaped chicken?
KFC Spain has kicked off a new marketing campaign that leans on the recent digital-only Grand Theft Auto VI release. In 2026, gamers have become numb to digital-only releases, piles of early bugs, and multiple layers of DRM. However, as GTA 6 is such a highly anticipated release, folks are still entitled to moan about the physical Blu-ray-style case, which opens to reveal absolutely no physical media at all, just a vacant plastic hub and a redeemable online code. KFC Spain is putting things right, as best as it can, by giving away a free fried chicken disc to those bringing their empty game cases to select outlets in the country.
'The Replacement Disc' campaign is a pretty simple proposition. You can buy and enjoy your GTA 6 release now, but on December 19 and 20 from 4:00 PM to 8:00 PM, take your empty game case down to KFC to get a free KFC disc. Branches where you can get this freebie food are located in major Spanish cities like Madrid, Barcelona, Valencia, Malaga, and Zaragoza.
The KFC disc will be formed from a piece of crunchy coated fried chicken, of course. While it surely will taste better than a platter of polycarbonate with a reflective metal alloy layer, it is only a substitute in spirit. We don't recommend you put greasy food directly in your game's case, even though it is basically useless. Definitely don't put your chicken disc anywhere near your console's optical media slot, if it has one.
GTA 6, released on November 19, is already a barnstorming success. The latest in this seminal series brought in US$3.79 billion in retail sales on its first day, publisher Rockstar Games said. That's about 5x the revenue of its predecessor. An incredible 32.5 million units were sold before release, and broke records across all platforms. So, it is canny for KFC to hitch its marketing wagon to this game, in such an unofficial but knowing social media-friendly way.
KFC has something of a track record of marketing off the back of tech and gaming culture. Its most famous tech adventure is probably the KFC Chicken Bucket Console. But more recently, last year, it teamed up with Asus to release some top-of-the-line burgers made from Wagyu beef with ROG branding.

articles.title: Far Eye helps reduce Flipkart logistics expenses by 6%
articles.text:
Far Eye helps reduce Flipkart logistics expenses by 6%
Far Eye says its logistics platform has helped Flipkart Wholesale cut logistics costs by 6%, reduce vehicle deployment by 8% and lower vehicle idle time by 10% through better routing, dispatch and fleet optimisation across its pan-India operations.
AI-powered enterprise SaaS Far Eye on Sunday said it has helped ecommerce major Flipkart's B2B cash-and-carry market place, Flipkart Wholesale, slash its logistics spend by 6% besides an 8% reduction in vehicle deployment pan-India.
This has enabled Flipkart Wholesale to improve fleet productivity without compromising delivery efficiency, reducing vehicle idle time by 10%, Far Eye said in a statement.
The improvements come from digitising and connecting dispatch, routing, compliance and payment collection processes across a network comprising 26 stores and one cross-dock, it said.
Flipkart Wholesale's network processes more than 200,000 orders and about 195,000 vehicle assignments a month.
The platform said it now supports the movement of goods across this network through a unified digital workflow, replacing largely manual and fragmented dispatch processes.
Far Eye said it also brought optimisation to match vehicle deployment to operational need, along with automated e-way bill generation, thus removing manual work from a compliance-heavy step.
All these initiatives resulted in 8% fewer vehicles across pan-India operations, with no impact on delivery efficiency, 6% lower total logistics spend, through better routing, dispatch discipline and fleet optimisation and 10% lower vehicle idle time, as planning and deployment improved fleet productivity, among others, it said.
India's general trade ecosystem of more than 1.4 crore kirana stores accounts for an estimated 75-80% of the country's FMCG sales. Procurement in this market is moving online.
The government-backed DigiDukaan initiative on ONDC has already connected more than 21,000 retailers with over 450 brands across three cities. As ordering gets easier, the pressure moves to what happens after the order is placed, the platform said.

articles.title: À l'occasion du Black Friday 2026, ces écouteurs Apple notés 5/5 passent à 188 €
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 : Les écouteurs sans fil Apple AirPods Pro 3 "5 étoiles" à 188,00 €
Actuellement notés 5 étoiles par notre rédaction, les Apple AirPods Pro 3 se distinguent par une restitution audio immersive et une réduction de bruit particulièrement performante. Pour le Black Friday, leur prix tombe à 188,00 € chez Amazon, soit une baisse d'environ 10 % et 19,93 € d'économie.
Apple fait évoluer ses écouteurs sans fil avec les Apple AirPods Pro 3 en adoptant un format intra-auriculaire plus marqué et une orientation pensée pour l'activité sportive. Ce modèle met l'accent sur l'immersion sonore et le traitement des bruits extérieurs. L'ensemble avait convaincu notre laboratoire.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, le tarif descend à 188,00 € chez Amazon, soit environ 10 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours (207,93 €). Cette baisse de prix permet d'économiser 19,93 €.
Réduction de bruit et autonomie en hausse dans notre test complet
Ces écouteurs sans fil se distinguent par une atténuation très efficace des sons ambiants, utile pour s'isoler dans les transports ou les espaces partagés. Notre laboratoire a mesuré une autonomie de 8 heures et 40 minutes avec la réduction de bruit active enclenchée, ce qui permet d'enchaîner une journée complète d'écoute sans passer par le boîtier. Sans cette fonction, la durée d'utilisation atteint 10 heures.
Apple AirPods Pro 3
Points forts
- Restitution précise, profonde et immersive.
- L'une des meilleures réduction de bruit.
- Très bon confort, excellent maintien.
- Résistants à l'eau et à la transpiration (IP57).
- Kit mains-libres de haut vol.
- Très riches en fonctionnalités.
Points faibles
- Sonorité moins équilibrée que sur les AirPods Pro 2.
- Conception intra-auriculaire clivante.
- Expérience utilisateur tronquée sur Android.
- Régression de l'autonomie totale.
Une conception pensée pour le sport et des fonctions avancées
Grâce à leur certification IP57, les AirPods Pro 3 résistent à l'eau et à la transpiration, ce qui autorise une utilisation intensive sous la pluie ou durant les séances d'entraînement physique. Le kit mains-libres assure des conversations vocales intelligibles pour vos interlocuteurs, même dans un environnement sonore animé. Le rendu audio se révèle toutefois moins équilibré que sur la génération précédente, un profil qui conviendra surtout à ceux qui privilégient une restitution sonore chaleureuse et dynamique.
Samsung Galaxy Buds4 Pro : l'autre option face au Apple AirPods Pro 3
Les Samsung Galaxy Buds4 Pro s'adressent en priorité aux utilisateurs de smartphones de la marque sud-coréenne. Ils proposent une signature sonore plus naturelle et un confort soigné, mais leur réduction de bruit atténue moins bien les fréquences médiums et leur autonomie reste en retrait par rapport à celle du modèle d'Apple.
Le tarif des Samsung Galaxy Buds4 Pro est inférieur de 28,01 € à celui des Apple AirPods Pro 3, mais ces derniers conservent l'avantage grâce à leur note actuelle de 5/5 et une isolation phonique bien supérieure.
Samsung Galaxy Buds4 Pro
Points forts
- Rendu sonore équilibré et naturel.
- Belle précision des basses et médiums.
- Excellent confort, format léger et compact.
- Bonne réduction du bruit, micros efficaces.
- Multiples fonctions, certification IP57.
Points faibles
- Légère brillance dans l'aigu.
- ANC perfectible dans le médium.
- Connectivité limitée hors univers Samsung.
- Pas d'app sur iOS.
- Autonomie correcte, sans plus.

articles.title: Sabemos que entrenar sin descanso perjudica al cuerpo. Ahora han descubierto qué puede ocurrir también en el cerebro
articles.text:
La norma que rige ahora mismo el ejercicio es la necesidad de esforzarnos para romper el equilibrio del organismo y descansar lo justo que permita reconstruirlo más fuerte. Pero cuando la balanza se inclina demasiado tiempo hacia la carga y la recuperación brilla por su ausencia, aparece el síndrome de sobreentrenamiento que castiga al músculo, al metabolismo y al sistema inmunitario. Pero ahora se ha visto que también afecta al cerebro.
Está estudiado. El trabajo, publicado en la revista Neuroscience, tenía como objetivo conocer exactamente qué ocurre en el hipocampo cuando el ejercicio pasa de un estímulo saludable a una auténtica sobrecarga crónica. Y esta zona del cerebro es bastante interesante, puesto que está encargada de la memoria, la respuesta al estrés o la regulación emocional.
Cómo lo hicieron. Para determinar el efecto de la sobrecarga a la hora de entrenar, los investigadores apostaron por trabajar con ratones macho a los que dividieron en dos escenarios. Por un lado, expusieron a estos animales a un esfuerzo puntual hasta el límite y, por el otro, a un programa prolongado diseñado para imitar la saturación que sufre un deportista de élite.
Si nos centramos en el esfuerzo puntual hasta llegar al agotamiento, se pudo ver que inmediatamente después del esfuerzo los niveles de dopamina subieron en el hipocampo, mientras que las enzimas que la fabrican comenzaron a disminuir para poder compensar el pico y volver a tener unos niveles normales.
Con mucha carga. Aquí la cosa cambia completamente, puesto que tras poner a los animales a entrenar en cinta con una intensidad creciente y sin apenas descanso, se detectó un gran desajuste metabólico. En concreto, se vio cómo los niveles de dopamina comenzaron a aumentar como antes, pero también la enzima que se encarga de fabricarla, por lo que no había un esfuerzo por tratar de compensar algo que estaba descontrolado y que predisponía a un aumento de dopamina sin control.
La serotonina. Para los investigadores, lo más importante no es el aumento de la dopamina, sino que la serotonina se mantuvo estable en ambas situaciones del experimento. Y esto es importante porque, durante décadas, la llamada hipótesis serotoninérgica de la fatiga central sostuvo que el agotamiento mental tras el ejercicio prolongado se debía a un aumento de la serotonina cerebral. Pero con el tiempo esto evolucionó para explicarlo con un cociente entre serotonina y dopamina, que hace que un alto valor favorezca la fatiga, mientras que uno más bajo se asocie a un estado de activación.
En los ratones sometidos a ocho semanas de entrenamiento extremo, la serotonina no varió, pero al mantenerse elevada la dopamina, el cociente serotonina/dopamina cayó durante el periodo de descanso. Dicho de otro modo: el sistema nervioso parecía incapaz de bajar las revoluciones cuando el cuerpo necesitaba recuperarse.
Es un problema. Con estos resultados encima de la mesa, se puede presuponer que un exceso de ejercicio sin el conveniente descanso puede dejar al cerebro "atascado a toda marcha" pudiendo generar ansiedad o irritabilidad. Aunque hay muchas dudas encima de la mesa, ya que los investigadores no evaluaron los efectos en el sueño o en los niveles de alerta de los ratones.

articles.title: « Welcome to Vice City » : Miami se met aux couleurs de GTA 6, et tout le monde n'apprécie pas
articles.text:
La série de jeux vidéo Grand Theft Auto a pour habitude de se dérouler dans une version parodique et satirique des États-Unis et GTA VI ne fait pas exception. Le dernier opus de Rockstar Games se déroule à Leonida, une Floride à peine déguisée dont la ville principale, Vice City, reprend largement les traits de Miami. Plutôt que de prendre ses distances avec une série connue pour ses braquages et ses fusillades, la métropole a choisi d’en profiter. Comme le rapporte l’Associated Press, le comté de Miami-Dade a conclu avec Rockstar Games un accord de 3,9 millions de dollars, qui comprend notamment un immense panneau « Welcome to Vice City » sur le toit du Kaseya Center, la salle des Miami Heat.
L’enceinte a d’ailleurs accueilli mercredi dernier, à la veille de la sortie du jeu, une soirée « A Night in Vice City ». Les joueurs du Heat ont évolué sur un parquet blanc, rose et bleu orné d’un « I love Vice City », vêtus d’un maillot spécial, tandis que les fast-foods fictifs du jeu, Cluckin’ Bell et Burger Joint, s’invitaient aux buvettes. Les villes de Miami et de Miami Beach ont aussi signé leurs propres accords de promotion, Rockstar a commandé des fresques dans le quartier de Wynwood, et le club E11EVEN s’est rebaptisé NINE1NINE, comme son double virtuel.
 Introducing the Vice City hardwood 🏀
See it for one night only, tomorrow vs Milwaukee. https://t.co/ZBpxND08hO
— Miami HEAT (@MiamiHEAT) November 17, 2026
Un jeu qui récompense le crime ?
Cette lune de miel ne fait toutefois pas l’unanimité. La shérif du comté, Rosie Cordero-Stutz, s’est opposée à l’utilisation de ressources publiques pour promouvoir un jeu qui récompense le crime, y compris la violence contre les forces de l’ordre. Conseiller municipal de Miami Beach, ville qui a dépensé des millions de dollars pour reprendre le contrôle du Spring Break, David Suarez refuse lui aussi d’« associer notre marque à quelque chose dont nous essayons si désespérément de nous éloigner depuis quelques années ». Sa collègue Monica Matteo-Salinas juge au contraire ces craintes exagérées : selon elle, la ville « peut miser sur ce matériel promotionnel, qui ne dure que six semaines, sans pour autant cautionner le jeu vidéo lui-même et les actions qui s’y déroulent ».
« Je ne peux peut-être pas faire ça dans la vraie vie, mais je peux clairement le faire dans GTA. » Un fan de la série à Miami, cité par l’AP
Une Floride reproduite avec soin
Si Miami se reconnaît autant dans Vice City, c’est que Rockstar a fait ses devoirs : ses équipes ont sillonné la ville et les Keys, survolé les Everglades et interrogé des habitants, dont d’anciens policiers et d’anciens membres de gangs. Un travail salué par Julie Fornary, guide pour la Miami Design Preservation League, pour qui aucune concession n’a été faite sur les néons et les façades Art déco d’Ocean Drive. « Nous avons le clinquant, mais aussi le crasseux. […] C’est le Miami que nous connaissons tous, nous qui vivons ici », résume-t-elle.
À lire aussi : GTA 6 : voici la façon la moins chère d’y jouer
L’engouement est tel aux quatre coins du monde qu’il se mesure aussi côté voyage. Selon Expedia, les recherches d’hébergement à Miami ont bondi de 55 % depuis la diffusion de la bande-annonce, le 15 octobre, par rapport à la même période l’an dernier, et celles pour Panama City, la station balnéaire qui a inspiré la ville de Port Gelhorn, de 65 %. Le groupe rattache ce phénomène à l’une des tendances de son rapport Horizons 2027, les séjours placés sous le signe du « retour à l’enfance », où les voyageurs troquent les programmes millimétrés contre des escapades ludiques et sans obligation. « Avec la sortie d’un titre aussi culte, on voit à quel point le besoin de déconnecter du quotidien et de retrouver une forme d’insouciance est fort chez les adultes », explique Xavier Rousselou, porte-parole d’Expedia.

articles.title: Activision Filing Describes NPCs That Learn How to React From Your Voice Chat
articles.text:
Sunday, November 22nd 2026
Activision Filing Describes NPCs That Learn How to React From Your Voice Chat
We have seen some unusual patents in the video game industry before, such as Sony's neckband that blows air on players, and Microsoft's pitch for ads during pauses. However, this one from Activision is unusual for a different reason. The application is titled "Methods and Systems for Applying Machine Learning to Generate Gameplay Audio," and was published on November 12, first spotted by Patentlyze. It describes a system that records how human players react over voice chat to specific game events, such as landing a kill or getting killed. That audio is then used to train a neural network after being matched to the events that triggered it, and the result is fed to NPCs. 
The goal is to train NPCs to have "human-like" reactions to in-game events, and those NPCs can be teammates or enemies. The filing mentions voice apps like Discord and TeamSpeak as possible sources for voice data, and apparently it's going to use timestamps so that the voice data from the players can be matched to in-game events. It shouldn't take much digging to get to the obvious problem with this method. Training an AI model on human reactions, especially using voice chat in emotionally charged gaming scenarios, is not really a great idea. Similar experiments have been run in the past, and almost every single one had to be shut down quickly after the AI crossed the line into offensive territory.Activision has seemingly given the problem some thought, at least. The filing includes a module to strip out abusive or offensive content, and also describes per-player profiles that can be tailored to specific players. However, we have seen in the past how users have been able to bypass safety measures on AI models, so this is not a foolproof solution. Moreover, the filing doesn't say how players would consent to have their voice chats recorded and used to train AI models. There's also no game cited, but it's reasonable to think of Call of Duty as the obvious candidate. This patent application is a continuation of an earlier one that goes back to December 2022. Sony has filed for NPCs that adapt to your playing style too, but as with most patents, there's no guarantee that this will ever turn into a real product.
Sources:
				Patentlyze, 				via Insider Gaming			
	
	
	
		
	
		
6 Comments on Activision Filing Describes NPCs That Learn How to React From Your Voice Chat
There's been several games in the past that tried using voice commands to control a character or at least activate abilities/perform orders or command teammates.
We're now at the point that it's almost viable; caveat being that the game would either need a second GPU to run a localized AI instance, or be online-only for it. Still, it'd be interesting to see what results out of it.
Off-hand:
Lifeline (PS2) was a JRPG game where you controlled the character almost entirely via voice command. It was too ahead of its time; because while the combat and cutscenes were decent, the voice recognition was subpar. Still, it gained a small but dedicated cult following who've tried to improve the voice recognition on PC.
Binary Domain (PS3/X360) was a 3rdPS game where if you had a headset, you could give basic commands and your teammates would respond to them; such as "Cover me!" or "Fall back!" or "Heal up!". However again, the voice recognition system was still primitive compared to basic PC talk-to-text dictation recognition and it didn't always work.
Skyrim's Xbox 360/X1 w/ Kinect compatibility allowed players to actually yell out some of the Dragonborn abilities to activate them, and later mods via PC allowed players to basically speak entire dialogue while interacting with NPCs.
Most recently is that silly multiplayer game where players cast spells they collect by voicing it out, with even a big area spell named DOOM that was activated by just saying DOOM.

articles.title: Netflix lanzará en marzo de 2027 su plan con anuncios en Colombia y Perú
articles.text:
Netflix lanzará su plan de suscripción con anuncios en Colombia y Perú en marzo de 2027, según la carta que la compañía presentó a sus accionistas el 20 de octubre ante la Comisión de Valores de Estados Unidos (SEC). Hasta ahora, no informó el precio ni el día exacto.
La carta indica que el servicio llegará a 15 países nuevos durante 2027. La primera tanda de lanzamientos será en marzo y reunirá a nueve países de Europa, Medio Oriente y África, además de Colombia, Perú y Nueva Zelanda.
Los nueve países de esa región son Austria, Bélgica, Dinamarca, Irlanda, los Países Bajos, Noruega, Polonia, Suecia y Suiza, según la lista que Netflix difundió en una presentación para anunciantes. La carta describe a Nueva Zelanda como una incorporación respecto del anuncio previo de la empresa.
En mayo de 2026, durante su presentación anual para anunciantes, Netflix había incluido a Colombia y Perú entre los 15 mercados de 2027, pero sin una fecha. La directora de Publicidad de la compañía, Amy Reinhard, habló de marzo en septiembre, durante un evento del sector en Brasil, según Produ.
Qué se sabe del precio y qué falta
Netflix no publicó cuánto costará el plan en pesos colombianos ni en soles. Tampoco detalló cuántos anuncios verá el suscriptor ni qué condiciones tendrá, por ejemplo, para descargar contenidos. La carta a los accionistas se limita a confirmar el calendario.
En Colombia, la plataforma vende hoy solo planes sin anuncios: el Básico cuesta COP 18.900 al mes, el Estándar COP 32.900 y el Premium COP 50.900, según Valora Analitik, que cita la página oficial de la empresa.
El medio calculó que, si Netflix aplica la proporción de otros mercados, el plan Estándar con anuncios costaría entre el 42% y el 60% del Estándar sin publicidad, lo que equivaldría a entre COP 14.000 y COP 19.700. Es una estimación del medio, no un precio de la empresa.
Valora Analitik recordó que en Estados Unidos, España y Brasil Netflix retiró después el plan Básico sin publicidad, de modo que la opción con anuncios quedó como la de entrada. No hay confirmación de que ocurra lo mismo en Colombia o Perú.
Brasil y México ya tienen el plan
El plan con anuncios ya funciona en Brasil y México. En mayo, Netflix informó que supera los 35 millones de usuarios activos mensuales en Brasil y los 28 millones en México, según la agencia peruana Andina. En todo el mundo, la compañía contó más de 250 millones de espectadores mensuales de esa modalidad.
Valora Analitik señaló que Argentina, por ahora, no ofrece este plan. La carta de Netflix no menciona al país entre los mercados de 2027.
La publicidad, un negocio que Netflix ajustó a la baja
La expansión llega junto con una corrección. En la misma carta, Netflix redujo su previsión de ingresos publicitarios de 2026 a unos USD 2.700 millones, frente a los cerca de USD 3.000 millones que esperaba antes. La empresa lo atribuyó a un despliegue algo más lento de algunas herramientas de publicidad.
En la conferencia con analistas, ejecutivos de Netflix dijeron que en mercados más nuevos, entre ellos Colombia, lo más importante es aumentar la cantidad de miembros, según la transcripción de la reunión que recoge PPC Land.

articles.title: The best apps to make new friends right now | TechCrunch
articles.text:
In recent years, people have been increasingly looking for new ways to form platonic connections, as loneliness and social isolation have become more prevalent.
In 2023, the U.S. Surgeon General went so far as to label this issue a public health crisis. Remote workers, who miss the everyday interactions found in an office, and younger individuals eager to create their adult social circles based on shared interests and hobbies, are among those seeking meaningful friendships.
Thanks to online dating apps, the stigma associated with finding connections online has largely faded away. This has welcomed a new wave of apps focused on fostering friendships and building local communities.
According to estimates from Appfigures, over a dozen local-focused friendship apps have collectively generated approximately $16 million in consumer spending in the U.S. so far this year. Some notable examples include Timeleft, Meet5, and Bumble’s BFF. Additionally, these apps have garnered approximately 4.3 million downloads thus far in 2025.
The apps aim to provide a less awkward solution than, for instance, approaching a stranger at the gym or local café and trying to strike up a conversation. These platforms clearly indicate that everyone using the app is looking for the same thing — friendship, not romance — making it much less intimidating to initiate conversations.
From major players like Meetup to newer ones like 222, there are plenty of apps that cater to the growing demand for meaningful friendships. We’ve compiled a list of them for you to try out.
222
The app 222 is an iOS-only social events platform that facilitates in-person meetups by pairing a group of strangers based on their personality test results. The app sends invitations to nearby public social events, such as wine bars and comedy clubs. There is then a vetting process, and selected participants are notified on the day of the event. A bonus for those who feel socially anxious: You’re allowed to bring a plus-one.
The service charges a $22.22 curation fee or a monthly subscription for the same price.
Bumble BFF
Dating giant Bumble is among the more established players to enter the friendship space, launching its friend-finding feature in 2016, which then spun out into a stand-alone app in 2023. The friend-making app has recently undergone a significant redesign, with an increased emphasis on facilitating group meetups, catering to users’ desires to grow their social circles.
BFF is available for free download on iOS and Android devices.
Clyx
Clyx is another emerging app in the group-based social networking landscape, with a strong focus on discovering local events. The social platform helps users find community events by integrating data from platforms like Ticketmaster and TikTok. Additionally, Clyx allows users to upload their contact lists, helping them see which events their friends plan to attend. The app also includes a feature that recommends other users to connect with at these events.
As of now, Clyx operates exclusively in two cities: Miami and London. However, it has plans to expand to additional areas in the near future, with New York City and São Paulo at the top of the list. The app is available on the App Store and Google Play Store.
Crowdier
Crowdier is a new group social app that lets friend groups connect with others. Users can create a group of 2-5 friends and browse other groups to arrange hangouts in person.
To initiate a match, users can “Wave” at groups they like, and if those groups wave back, they can plan in a shared chat. A match requires the majority of both groups to agree. For example, 2 people in a 4-person group needs to say yes.
The app is available for free on iOS and Android devices.
Les Amís
Les Amís is a friendship app tailored for women, transgender, and LGBTQ+ individuals that leverages AI to match users based on similar interests and encourages participation in local events, such as pottery classes, book clubs, and wine tastings. Matches are made every Monday, allowing users to chat and plan meetups later in the week.
Available on iOS and Android, Les Amís serves cities across Europe, including Amsterdam, Barcelona, Berlin, Madrid, Paris, and Stockholm. In the U.S., the app is available in Austin and New York, with plans to expand to Boston, Miami, and Los Angeles.
The app uses a paid membership model that varies by city, with fees of $70 in New York and €55 in Amsterdam.
Meetup
The local event-discovery platform has been around since 2002, helping millions of users connect with others who share similar interests. Users can RSVP to events; join groups that cater to a variety of hobbies, professions, or social causes; and create their own groups and events. They can also chat with group members and post updates and photos from gatherings.
Meet5
This European community-building app recently launched in the U.S., targeting users over 40 who want to meet new people in their area and participate in group activities such as picnics, concerts, and hiking. Notably, in a short time, there have been around 777,000 U.S. downloads so far across the App Store and Google Play Store, according to Appfigures estimates.
Pie
Pie is another one of the newer social apps on the market. It features an AI-driven quiz designed to predict which users are most likely to be compatible with each other. Each person who RSVPs to a Pie event takes a brief personality assessment, and the algorithm organizes attendees into groups of six, who are then added to a group chat within the Pie app, allowing them to interact with each other before the event.
Currently, the app is only available in Austin, Chicago, and San Francisco. Users can download Pie from the App Store and Google Play Store.
Timeleft
Timeleft is a relatively new platform that helps you organize weekly dinner dates with groups of strangers. The app uses a special algorithm to match you with others, taking into account your age, gender, and personality. Users are matched with four other people, but they only learn minor details about them the night before, including their occupations and zodiac signs.
Dinners take place at a selected restaurant on Wednesday evenings at 7:00 p.m. To help everyone break the ice, the app offers a game with conversation starters. After dinner, there is an after-party at a local bar.
Users can book dinners online or through the app. In terms of pricing, it varies depending on the country and restaurant. Users pay for a ticket up front and are responsible for covering their own dinner and drinks.
Washed Up
Washed Up is a social event discovery app that launched in early 2026, designed for people in the Los Angeles area who want an easier way to find things to do and meet new people.
The app helps users discover local events, such as concerts, trivia nights, and comedy shows, while also giving them a built-in way to connect with others who plan to attend. Instead of going to events alone, users can create or join “plans,” which are small group meetups tied to specific events. Users can browse these plans and request to join, chat with the group, and add new friends, making it easier to show up to events with people rather than by themselves.
It’s available to download on the App Store.
Wyzr Friends
Wyzr Friends is an activity-based friendship app designed for adults 40 and older, catering to empty nesters, those who are divorced, and other users seeking to connect with like-minded individuals. Users can thumbs up or down potential friends and arrange in-person activities based on shared interests, such as going to the movies or hiking.
It’s available on iOS and Android devices in the U.S., Canada, Australia, Ireland, the Philippines, Singapore, and Mexico.
Mmotion
Mmotion is a newly launched friendship app that blends location tracking with social discovery to help users connect with people nearby and explore new bars and restaurants in their area. Upon joining, users can participate in interest-based groups — such as hiking, basketball, or art — view a map of active users, and send messages to those nearby. The app also highlights new places on the map, making it easy to find a restaurant or venue to try.
Mmotion is currently only available to users in New York City on iOS and Android devices. Users must first submit an application to be considered.
Synchrony
Launched in March 2026, Synchrony is a new social app tailored for neurodivergent adults. Founded by a mother of a son on the autism spectrum, it aims to create a supportive community through features like interest-based matching and two-step identity verification. This ensures that users engage safely, as both a user and a trusted person must verify personal details and a photo ID during registration.
A standout feature is Jesse, an optional AI communication tool that assists users in navigating conversations. The AI provides editable prompts to help express thoughts, clarifies conversations, and offers boundary-setting suggestions. While the incorporation of AI may raise concerns, there are guardrails built into Jesse, such as avoiding medical advice.
Users must pay a monthly subscription of $44.99 after a 30-day free trial. It’s available on iOS and Android devices.

articles.title: NFL Week 11 preview: 5 must-watch games you can't afford to miss this Sunday
articles.text:
NFL Week 11 preview: 5 must-watch games you can't afford to miss this Sunday
Here's our pick of the top five NFL Week 11 games – and who's showing them
Although nobody's yet been eliminated from the NFL 2026 playoffs, with every passing week the jeopardy is rising, and in Week 11 it's resulted in a not-so-Super Bowl meeting between Baltimore and Carolina, each of whom can ill-afford another defeat.
It's been a bad enough week for Detroit, what with losing Aidan Hutchinson for the rest of the campaign, and now the schedulers have conspired against them too. Not only are they coming off a long-haul flight, but they're returning to an unfavourable matchup against a well-rested Tampa Bay side.
Scroll down for our pick of the top five NFL Week 11 games – and who's showing them.
Ravens at Panthers
- Sunday, 1pm ET, Fox/Fox One (US)
Like a pair of bald men fighting over a comb, what this game lacks in quality it'll more than make up for with sheer desperation. The Panthers are solely in the playoff picture by virtue of leading the worst division in football. One slip and it could all go up in smoke. The Ravens are on the brink of elimination after losing to the previously winless Chargers, and worst of all, their ever-reliable running game has hit a wall. It's not quite the Super Bowl, but it'll feel like it to both teams.
Buccaneers at Lions
- Sunday, 1pm ET, CBS/Paramount+ (US)
In any previous week, this would have been a total mismatch, but the Buccaneers' bye and the Lions' European jetlag have made this very interesting. Even with Hutchinson helming the defense, Jared Goff and Jahmyr Gibbs have been having to put up unsustainable numbers just to grind out wins. With the two-time Pro Bowl defensive end sidelined, having torn his ACL celebrating too hard, Detroit's defense just got a whole lot worse. Although it isn't clear if Baker Mayfield will recover from his foot injury in time, regardless of who suits up at quarterback, the Bucs are going to run it. Their rushing offense is by far the best in the league.
Jaguars at Giants
- Sunday, 4.25pm ET, CBS/Paramount+ (US) | FREE on 5 (UK), Virgin Media Play (IRE), 7Plus (AUS) & TVNZ+ (NZ)
The Jaguars are a juggernaut, riding a three-game winning streak and boasting a +125 points differential – the best in the NFL – and at MetLife Stadium they'll unleash Super Bowl-winning defensive tackle Jordan Davis and Pro Bowl safety Jessie Bates. That'll be worth seeing in itself, but with little between the Giants, Cowboys and Commanders in the NFC East, Big Blue's hold on a playoff spot is far from assured. With their schedule set to get a lot tougher from here on in, an upset on Sunday would be a huge step towards ending the longest drought in the conference and winning a first division title since 2011.
Vikings vs 49ers
- Sunday, 8.20pm ET, NBC/Peacock (US)
A genuine blockbuster between one of the best defensive teams in the NFL and one of its best offensive teams feels all the more special because it's the first game in four years to take place at Mexico City's iconic Estadio Azteca. Better still, both sides will feel that they have the edge. Kirk Cousins took no time to re-connect with Justin Jefferson and improve Minnesota's offense immeasurably, while Brock Purdy is precisely the type of metronomic quarterback that Brian Flores' vaunted defense could struggle to get to grips with.
Bengals at Commanders
- Monday, 8.15pm ET, ESPN, ESPN2/ESPN Unlimited (US)
After five straight wins, nobody's hotter than the Bengals right now. And the bonkers thing is, they've only got a Plan A, but Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are executing it so well they're just scything through opponents. While Burrow leads the NFL in passing yards, passing touchdowns and completion percentage, the Commanders have the second-worst passing defense in the league. However, with their season on the line they rose to the occasion last weekend, Jayden Daniels brushing off two late interceptions to engineer a 71-yard scoring drive, after the defense twice saved his blushes. At home and in primetime, with the stakes once again sky-high, don't rule out another heroic effort.
