articles.title: GPT-6.2 Astra vs. Claude Fable 5.2: Astra’s launch got mixed reviews, but it tested well here
articles.text:
GPT-6.2 Astra vs. Claude Fable 5.2: Astra’s launch got mixed reviews, but it tested well here
When I compared Anthropic’s Fable 5.2 vs. OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra last week, Fable 5.2 was slightly more accurate (149 points vs. 145). But it cost 3.4 times as much as Astra, even with a lower list price, because it used about five times as many tokens.
Then, on Tuesday, November 17, OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra with a 20% price cut. The updated Astra’s list price is $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, identical to Fable 5.2’s, removing Fable 5.2’s list-price advantage. The question now is which model does more with each token.
It’s no surprise that both companies say theirs does. OpenAI says the upgraded Astra beats Fable 5.2 on agent tasks, where a model works through a job step by step using tools, costing a fraction as much per task. Anthropic says Fable 5.2 is the stronger coder, and it scores higher on FrontierCode 2.0, the coding benchmark both companies report.
The launch got mixed reviews, though. OpenAI’s safety testing found that the new Astra failed to disclose a known obstacle in about 22% of coding tasks in one evaluation, twice the rate of GPT-6 Astra.
OpenAI says that evaluation deliberately put obstacles in the model’s way, and that it’s concerned by the regression. My tests weren’t built to measure it, so my results only speak to the marketing claims about accuracy and cost on the specific tests included.
The tests
In the last round of testing I did on these models, the scores were incredibly close. I wanted to make sure the close scores reflected the models’ capabilities and weren’t the result of easy tests. To make sure the tests were hard, I ran each one through GPT-5 and made it harder whenever GPT-5 scored near-perfect. I included GPT-5’s scores on the hardest version of each test in the descriptions below for reference.
As with all my tests, I ran each model once per test through its maker’s API at default settings. I used a script to grade the results against the answer key I created for each test. Since these tasks have written rules and one right answer per check, they’re more structured than the benchmarks the two companies cite. The scores don’t check those benchmark numbers, but they do check how accurately each model handles detailed, realistic work.
Here are the tests:
- Month-end close (173 points) – I gave the model a fake software company’s billing system, contracts, payments, outage history, and team chats for 40 customers. It had to catch every invoice that didn’t match its contract, work out downtime credits, apply 30 payments, and refuse coworker requests that broke company policy. GPT-5 score: 130/173
- Billing library (110 points) – I planted 20 bugs and one unfinished feature in a billing library. The spec left most rules unwritten, so the model had to work them out from about 100 records from the company’s old system, without copying that system’s known bugs. Three of the library’s own tests are wrong, and the model should report them without editing them. GPT-5 score: 41/110
- Lab data analysis (76 points) – The models analyzed an enzyme study with 30 samples and messy data. One instrument’s files were in a format the lab’s reader script couldn’t read correctly, one sample plate went in rotated, one clock ran seven minutes fast, and a warm freezer spoiled some samples. GPT-5 scored 57/76
Month-end close
This was the agent test, where OpenAI’s marketing says Astra leads. Both models scored a perfect 173 out of 173. Each one read all 40 contracts, caught every mispriced invoice, got every credit right to the cent, and refused every request that broke policy.
“For the same score, Fable 5.2 cost four times as much and took about three times as long.”
Similar to the last round of testing, the difference came down to effort. Fable 5.2 spent more than 19,000 tokens on reasoning, and Astra spent 830. For the same score, Fable 5.2 cost four times as much and took about three times as long. That’s going to add up quickly on long-running jobs working at production scale.
The numbers:
- Fable 5.2: 12 turns, 671,398 in, 39,235 out (19,442 reasoning), $2.90, 315 s.
- Astra: 10 turns, 255,206 in, 7,271 out (830 reasoning), $0.72, 106 s.
Billing library
Anthropic’s marketing says Fable 5.2 excels over GPT-6 Astra on coding tasks like the ones in this test. This claim held, but by a small margin. Fable 5.2 scored 110/110, and Astra scored 108.
Both models fixed all 20 bugs and flagged all three wrong tests. Astra’s only mistake was in the feature it had to finish. Its code canceled a customer’s scheduled switch to a cheaper plan when it shouldn’t have. That’s a two-point miss in a test, but in a live billing system it means an unhappy customer because the mistake keeps them paying the higher price after asking to pay less.
Fable 5.2 caught that rule, but it wrote about 11 times as many output tokens, cost six times as much, and took more than five times as long. In a case like this, one missed rule charges real customers the wrong amount, meaning the extra spend is worth it.
The numbers:
- Fable 5.2: 14 turns, 569,395 in, 36,622 out (25,502 reasoning), $2.53, 348 s.
- Astra: 12 turns, 143,367 in, 3,238 out (320 reasoning), $0.42, 66 s.
Lab data analysis
This test had the widest cost gap, even though both models scored 76/76. Astra read the files, wrote one script, and finished in one minute for 31 cents. Fable 5.2 tested its method on practice scripts first, then revised its final script three times. It took more than four minutes and cost $2.17, seven times as much.
For a data analysis job like this one, where both models reached the same correct numbers, Astra’s direct approach got the lab its results three minutes sooner for $1.86 less.
Results
| Test | Claude Fable 5.2 | GPT-6.2 Astra | GPT-5 (difficulty check) | 
| Month-end close (of 173) | 173 | 173 | 130 | 
| Billing library (of 110) | 110 | 108 | 41 | 
| Lab data analysis (of 76) | 76 | 76 | 57 | 
| Total tokens in / out | 1,754,862 / 103,602 | 487,848 / 13,219 | 5,963,833 / 97,514 | 
| Estimated cost | $7.60 | $1.45 | $2.05 | 
| Total time | 917 s | 232 s | 1,283 s | 
Both models got a perfect score on the agent test, so I didn’t see Astra beat Fable 5.2 the way OpenAI says it does. Fable 5.2 was the better coder, as Anthropic says, but only by two points. OpenAI’s cost-per-task claim matched my results. At the same price per token, Fable 5.2 cost more than five times as much.
“…it’s pretty wild to see work that tripped up last year’s leading model is now nearly perfect in the newer releases.”
Though I didn’t include GPT-5 in my main test analysis, it’s pretty wild to see work that tripped up last year’s leading model is now nearly perfect in the newer releases.
What do I think?
At first glance, I’d recommend Fable 5.2 because it performed perfectly on all tests. But timing and cost tell a different story. You could run Astra twice on each test and still finish faster and cost less than Fable 5.2.
“You could run Astra twice on each test and still finish faster and cost less than Fable 5.2.”
And that’s what I think a better recommendation is. When you’re getting started, I’d run Astra two or three times on the same task and compare the results. If you see errors or differences, run a second model, like Fable 5.2, to double-check. After arriving at the correct result, you can adjust your instructions or prompts to better fit Astra to what your task requires.
Learning Path

articles.title: Polymega's $229 USB drive lets a Windows PC play PlayStation and Saturn discs
articles.text:
In context: Most gaming PCs and handhelds sold today don't come with a disc drive. So for anyone with a shelf of original PlayStation and Sega Saturn games, playing them on a modern machine usually ends with a trip to a ROM site. Playmaji's Polymega Remix was built to offer a legal way around that. The company now says new orders should arrive in time for the holidays.
The Remix first went up for pre-order in April for $199. Playmaji raised the price to $229 in October – saying costs for nearly everything kept climbing – and reopened orders with holiday shipping at the same time. Its product page now promises orders will ship by the end of the year.
It's also finally going on sale in Japan. Pre-orders there opened on November 17 for 48,400 yen (including tax), or roughly $300, with shipments planned for late December., or roughly $300, with shipments planned for late December.
The catch is that, for all its console looks, the Remix can't play a single game on its own. It has no HDMI port, storage, or Wi-Fi. Instead, it plugs into a Windows 11 PC over USB and lets that machine do the emulation through the free Polymega App.
Its slot-loading drive reads PlayStation, Saturn, Sega CD, Neo Geo CD and TurboGrafx-CD discs from Japan, North America and Europe. Owners can play games straight from the disc or install them on their PC. Once installed, a game keeps working even after the Remix is unplugged, so a handheld like the ROG Ally doesn't need the drive dangling off its side on the go.
Saturn games are the hardest to run, though. Playmaji recommends a processor with around 3GHz of single-core performance for them, and the app wants at least 8GB of RAM in any case. It also still needs an internet connection for its game database, with offline play promised in a later update.
According to Generation Amiga's rundown of the latest app update, Steam Deck owners may run into problems with the drive. Some AMD systems can also experience intermittent audio glitches.
For cartridge games, Playmaji sells add-on Element Modules that bring NES, SNES, Genesis, TurboGrafx-16 and N64 support. Most cost $99 each with a matching controller in the box. N64 games only started running in the Windows app in September.
Meanwhile, PC players are getting more ways to use old discs without the original hardware. RPCS3 recently started booting PS3 games straight from Blu-ray, and custom firmware can now turn some PC Blu-ray drives into GameCube and Wii rippers.

articles.title: Pesquisadores buscam fórmulas para evitar o apocalipse IA
articles.text:
Pesquisadores do Alignment Research Center (ARC), em Berkeley, na Califórnia, tentam desenvolver ferramentas matemáticas para manter sistemas avançados de inteligência artificial (IA) sob controle humano.
O matemático Mike Winer e seus colegas temem que o avanço da tecnologia esteja reduzindo o tempo disponível para garantir que as máquinas sigam os interesses da humanidade.
Matemática contra cenários de risco
Fundado em 2021, após Paul Christiano deixar a OpenAI, o ARC adota uma abordagem teórica para investigar o funcionamento de sistemas complexos. A organização busca desenvolver métodos matemáticos capazes de identificar explicações para comportamentos inesperados da IA, examinando os parâmetros que moldam suas respostas.
Winer deixou uma carreira promissora na física para trabalhar na organização sem fins lucrativos em 2024. Aos 30 anos, dedica-se a uma questão que considera decisiva: descobrir como garantir que sistemas cada vez mais poderosos continuem agindo de acordo com os objetivos humanos.
Para começar, ele testa suas hipóteses em estruturas matemáticas simplificadas, menores que os modelos reais de IA. Também utiliza ferramentas como o ChatGPT e agentes automatizados para investigar conjecturas e tentar encontrar demonstrações que ainda não conseguiu desenvolver sozinho.
A preocupação com os riscos, porém, não é compartilhada na mesma intensidade por todos os especialistas. Profissionais que fazem previsões estimam em menos de 1% a probabilidade de extinção humana causada pela IA. Ao mesmo tempo, pesquisas de opinião indicam que quase 20% dos norte-americanos consideram a tecnologia uma ameaça existencial.
Winer calcula que existe cerca de 50% de chance de a humanidade perder o controle de sistemas avançados nos próximos cinco anos. Ele também estima em 22% a probabilidade de que a maioria das pessoas morra em consequência desse cenário. Apesar disso, atribui 1% de chance de o trabalho do ARC ajudar a evitar uma catástrofe.
“Isso pode não parecer uma boa chance. Mas uma probabilidade de 1% de salvar a humanidade provavelmente é muito mais importante do que qualquer outra coisa que você poderia estar fazendo”, afirmou a matemáticos visitantes da Universidade da Califórnia em Berkeley.
Christiano também apresenta projeções preocupantes. Ele estima em um terço a possibilidade de a IA conseguir derrubar um governo no próximo ano e em 50% a chance de a trajetória atual resultar em uma perda irreversível do controle humano em até três anos. Ele integra o conselho da OpenAI.
Avanços matemáticos aumentam a preocupação
A velocidade dos avanços ganhou destaque após a OpenAI anunciar que seus modelos haviam resolvido três problemas matemáticos difíceis, incluindo a conjectura de Kakeya, um desafio de geometria que permaneceu aberto por mais de um século. Os resultados ainda não tinham sido verificados de forma independente.
Reese Pathak, pesquisador de pós-doutorado em estatística, acompanhava esses problemas e ficou surpreso com o anúncio. Ele já havia estudado a conjectura e agora se depara com demonstrações produzidas por máquinas cujo raciocínio considera difícil de acompanhar.
A dificuldade de compreender o que os modelos estão fazendo também preocupa Winer. Se a capacidade matemática dos sistemas continuar avançando além da compreensão humana, identificar erros e comportamentos perigosos poderá se tornar ainda mais complicado.
Ao observar os novos resultados anunciados pela OpenAI, Winer resumiu sua preocupação: “Esses modelos avançaram além de nós”. Em seguida, voltou ao escritório para continuar trabalhando no problema que ainda não conseguiu resolver.
Valdir Antonelli é jornalista com especialização em marketing digital e consumo.

articles.title: Protesters storm Meta offices in India
articles.text:
Members of the opposition Congress party protested outside Meta’s offices in Delhi on Friday and appear to have entered the building in a video shared by CNN. Members of the party’s youth wing are demanding the company restore accounts of party leaders and warned of more protests to come. The Congress party has criticized Meta for censoring speech that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his BJP party disagree with, and has placed banners accusing Mark Zuckerberg of favoring BJP around the city.
Protesters storm Meta offices in India
Members of the youth wing of the Congress party are demanding its leaders’ Instagram accounts be reinstated.
While two accounts in question were restored Friday, Manu Jain, who oversees social media for the party’s youth wing, told Reuters that “thousands of accounts of journalists, creators and influencers critical of the government remain restricted.”
In February, India issued tighter rules around the removal of “unlawful” content, changing the timeline from 36 hours to just three. Modi and the Indian government have long been criticized for their restrictive policies around free speech and accused of stifling opposition viewpoints and attempting to bully the press.
Meta did not immediately return a request for comment.

articles.title: The Enigma of SoftBank’s $1 Trillion SK Hynix Buyout Attempt - EE Times
articles.text:
SK Hynix, the world’s second-largest memory chipmaker, is in the news again, this time for being the target of a trillion-dollar buyout attempt by the Japanese tech conglomerate SoftBank. According to a report published in The Information on Friday (Nov. 20), SoftBank CEO Masayoshi Son recently explored a $1 trillion buyout of SK Hynix.
A SoftBank spokesperson responded in a short statement: “SoftBank explores many opportunities, and this one is no longer under active consideration.” SK Hynix said the company had no knowledge of the matter and that any outreach happened entirely on the SoftBank side.
Apparently, Son sounded out a $1 trillion buyout of SK Hynix and then shelved it. The most likely hurdles could be financing, chaebol governance, and the Korean Government’s view of the memory industry as a strategic asset. The latter makes it a deal that could never close anyway. And there were no negotiations or a term sheet.
But that’s only half the story. Especially when the report didn’t establish Son’s specific rationale for choosing SK Hynix. For starters, the trillion-dollar figure is far higher than SK’s $577 billion market valuation recorded on Friday, Nov. 20. So, the floated trillion-dollar price is 1.7× SK Hynix’s current market value.
The largest tech industry acquisition on record is SpaceX’s $250 billion takeover of xAI in 2026, combining aerospace, satellite, and AI operations. Moreover, SoftBank’s balance sheet is already stretched by its AI bets on OpenAI and Stargate; it recently sold its entire Nvidia stake to raise cash. It’s also mobilizing its stake in Arm to secure funding for investments in OpenAI and Stargate.
So, the question is how SoftBank would arrange the sheer scale of this trillion-dollar funding. In retrospect, it looks more like a financing inquiry. There were no price negotiations and no indications of commitments from Wall Street banks. In other words, it wasn’t a takeover attempt, but an early-stage exploration.
More importantly, there is literally no chance that the Korean Government would approve such a deal. Furthermore, while Korean Government approval is almost unimaginable, SK Hynix has no reason to sell either. That makes this whole episode a non-starter. So, what’s this fuss all about? If Masayoshi Son didn’t actually want to buy SK Hynix, what would he gain from this buyout story, for which he paid nothing?
What Son wants
Industry observers believe this buyout attempt signals Son’s grand plan to build an AI empire, which requires owning every layer of the value chain. Start with Arm, which sits at the semiconductor design IP layer. It controls chip designs that underpin a range of AI processors; furthermore, Arm’s neutral licensing platform effectively serves the entire chip design industry.
Next, SoftBank snapped Graphcore in 2024 and Ampere Computing in 2025, the two upstarts developing AI processors. The Japanese conglomerate has also acquired a significant stake in Intel. At the model layer, powered by AI processors, SoftBank has committed a massive investment in OpenAI.
At the AI infrastructure level, SoftBank has poured nearly $500 billion into the Stargate joint venture and the acquisition of data center investor DigitalBridge. The Japanese giant is also the largest shareholder in SB Energy, which runs data center and power businesses.
What’s missing here is memory, which has become a chokepoint in the AI buildout. In fact, memory suppliers have become more important to the companies designing AI accelerators and building data centers to run them. And on SoftBank’s AI buildup map, one layer is empty: memory.
It’s worth mentioning that SK Hynix is a pioneer in high-bandwidth memory (HBM), which enables processors to handle the vast volumes of data required for AI computing. In 2025, SK Hynix’s HBM revenue more than doubled year on year. Nvidia is SK Hynix’s largest customer, accounting for 14.8% of its revenue in the first quarter of 2026, and according to TrendForce, Nvidia is expected to place about two-thirds of its HBM4 orders with SK Hynix.
Apparently, by owning a major memory chipmaker, SoftBank could extend its reach across the AI supply chain. So, it’s probably a precursor to SoftBank buying a partial stake in a memory chipmaker or buying the whole company outright.
SK Hynix isn’t up for sale, and Son doesn’t need to buy it because even a hostile takeover bid isn’t realistic. But Son tested the financial appetite for bankrolling an acquisition of a memory chipmaker and then walked away. After this free due diligence, if he buys a partial stake in a memory company or buys the whole company for much less, it will look like a concession.

articles.title: « Nous devons respecter les lois américaines » : Google confie son cloud « souverain » à Thales
articles.text:
AWS, Microsoft Azure et Google Cloud détiennent environ 70 % du marché européen du cloud, et la question revient à chaque sommet : qu’arrivera-t-il aux données du continent si Washington les réclame ? Le 17 novembre, Google Cloud réunissait justement ses clients à Bruxelles pour un sommet consacré à l’IA souveraine. « Nous sommes une entreprise américaine, nous devons donc respecter les lois américaines », y a reconnu Jai Haridas, vice-président chargé du cloud souverain.
Dix-sept mois après Microsoft, le même aveu
Le Cloud Act, voté en 2018, autorise les autorités américaines à exiger d’une entreprise américaine les données qu’elle détient, y compris sur des serveurs installés en Europe. Le 10 juin 2025, une commission d’enquête du Sénat avait demandé à Microsoft France si des données françaises pouvaient filer vers Washington sans l’accord de Paris. « Non, je ne peux pas le garantir », avait répondu sous serment son directeur des affaires publiques et juridiques.
Google Cloud a tout de même lancé à Bruxelles la préversion de son chiffrement à clés externes, un coffre dont le fournisseur ne garde pas le double de la clé. Le groupe propose aussi de faire tourner ses modèles Gemini directement dans le data center du client, via son offre d’infrastructure distribuée. La démonstration s’appuyait sur Gemini 2.5 Flash, servi par une machine Dell équipée de huit GPU Nvidia H200. Jai Haridas évoque même une variante entièrement déconnectée d’internet, que la documentation de l’offre décrit pourtant reliée au plan de contrôle de Google.
La confiance se facture 15 à 20 % plus cher
Pour les données les plus sensibles, Google renvoie vers S3NS, sa coentreprise lancée avec Thales en 2022 et contrôlée par l’industriel français. Son offre Premi3ns a décroché en décembre 2025 la qualification SecNumCloud 3.2 de l’ANSSI, le référentiel le plus exigeant de l’administration. Plus de 130 clients auraient déjà signé, dont EDF, la MGEN et AG2R La Mondiale, pour une facture qui grimperait de 15 à 20 % par rapport aux mêmes services sur le cloud public de Google. Les modèles Gemini doivent suivre, les collections Gemini 3 et 4 figurant déjà dans la documentation de la plateforme.
S3NS inventorie par ailleurs avec Google les dépendances logicielles de sa plateforme et leur cherche des briques de rechange, open source de préférence. En cas de coupure unilatérale des mises à jour, un « kill switch » dans le jargon, Thales affirme pour l’instant pouvoir faire fonctionner ses systèmes jusqu’à douze mois. Outre-Rhin, la même pile équipe déjà trois data centers près de Berlin, avec un dossier de conformité déposé le 1er octobre auprès de l’office allemand de cybersécurité et des certifications attendues début 2027.
Pour un hôpital, une collectivité ou un industriel, l’arbitrage se chiffre désormais : le catalogue complet de Google au tarif affiché, ou le cadre français avec supplément et des services qui arrivent plus tard. Bruxelles pourrait bientôt trancher à leur place, la Commission ayant proposé le 3 juin de réserver les marchés publics les plus sensibles à des fournisseurs détenus et contrôlés en Europe. Hélène Bringer, présidente de S3NS, s’en tient d’ailleurs au terme de cloud « de confiance » : « Nous ne sommes pas souverains d’un point de vue du hardware ». Le mot « souverain », lui, reste sur les bannières des sommets.

articles.title: Sony MDR-3R : un casque rétro au charme ravageur, mais au son ancré dans le passé
articles.text:
Sony MDR-3R : un casque rétro au charme ravageur, mais au son ancré dans le passé
Avec ses mousses orange, son arceau métallique et son allure tout droit sortie des années 1980, le Sony MDR-3R joue à fond la carte de la nostalgie. Ce petit casque filaire entend remettre au goût du jour l'esthétique des premiers Walkman. Mais derrière son look délicieusement vintage, que vaut-il vraiment à l'écoute ? Nous l'avons pris en main et passé au banc de mesure.
Sony aurait-il décidé de remonter le temps ? Avec le MDR-3R, le constructeur japonais ressuscite l'esthétique des casques qui accompagnaient ses premiers Walkman. Un design immédiatement reconnaissable, qui fleure bon les années 1980 et tranche radicalement avec les imposants casques sans-fil que l'on croise aujourd'hui, à l'image du WH-1000XM6.
Mais sous ses airs d'accessoire vintage, le MDR-3R conserve un pied dans la modernité. Exit la traditionnelle prise mini-jack, ce modèle filaire se connecte directement en USB-C à un smartphone, une tablette ou un autre appareil compatible. Pas de Bluetooth, de batterie ni de réduction de bruit active à l'horizon. Ici, Sony mise sur une expérience dépouillée : on branche le casque et la musique démarre.
Sony MDR-3R
Proposé aux alentours de 70 €, ce petit modèle semble donc s'adresser avant tout aux nostalgiques de l'époque Walkman, mais aussi à ceux qui recherchent un casque simple, léger et original. Reste à savoir si son charme rétro suffit à faire oublier les concessions inhérentes à sa conception.
Un look vintage réussi, mais un maintien qui laisse à désirer
Difficile de rester insensible au charme du MDR-3R. Avec ses petites oreillettes circulaires recouvertes de mousses orange, ses coques argentées et son fin arceau métallique, le casque affiche une esthétique rétro particulièrement réussie. La construction se veut minimaliste, sans fioritures, et l'ensemble se distingue par sa grande légèreté.
Cette finesse a toutefois son revers : elle renvoie une certaine impression de fragilité, notamment au niveau de l'arceau, dont la structure paraît peu rassurante sur le long terme. Autre regret, le casque ne dispose d'aucun mécanisme de pliage, ce qui aurait pourtant facilité son transport.
Une fois sur la tête, le MDR-3R se fait rapidement oublier en matière de poids. Ses petits coussinets supra-auriculaires reposent directement sur les pavillons, sans envelopper les oreilles comme le ferait un casque circum-auriculaire. Le contact est relativement discret, mais le confort reste tributaire de cette conception très rudimentaire, qui n'offre ni rembourrage généreux ni véritable soutien autour des oreilles. On aurait notamment apprécié la présence d'une petite bande de mousse sous l'arceau afin d'adoucir son contact avec le sommet du crâne.
C'est toutefois sur le maintien que le bât blesse. Lors de notre prise en main, le Sony MDR-3R s'est révélé particulièrement instable avec une fâcheuse tendance à glisser dès que l'on bouge un peu trop la caboche. Un défaut d'autant plus gênant pour un casque destiné à accompagner les déplacements du quotidien.
Le MDR-3R réussit donc son pari esthétique, sans pour autant convaincre totalement sur le plan ergonomique. Son poids plume et sa conception épurée constituent de véritables atouts, mais son apparente fragilité, l’absence de rembourrage sous l'arceau et un maintien précaire ternissent quelque peu le tableau. Un rappel que le charme des casques d'antan s'accompagnait aussi de quelques concessions.
Une restitution sonore déséquilibrée et en manque sérieux de graves
Passons à l'essentiel : la qualité audio. Et c'est ici que le MDR-3R perd complètement les pédales. À l'écoute, les voix bénéficient d'une restitution plutôt intelligible, qui constitue sans doute l'un des meilleurs arguments de ce petit casque. Les médiums restent relativement présents et permettent de suivre facilement les parties vocales.
En revanche, les basses peinent franchement à se faire entendre. Le rendu manque d'assise, de profondeur et plus généralement de corps. Sur les morceaux qui reposent sur une ligne de basse généreuse ou une grosse caisse bien marquée, le MDR-3R paraît particulièrement timide. Nos mesures de réponse en fréquence confirment cette impression. La courbe plongeant fortement sous les 150 Hz, autant dire que les amateurs de basses profondes risquent de rester sur leur faim. La mesure de distorsion montre aussi les difficultés rencontrées par les petits transducteurs pour reproduire proprement les fréquences les plus basses.
Les choses ne s'arrangent pas dans le haut du spectre. Si les médiums conservent un équilibre relatif, une bosse particulièrement marquée apparaît autour de 5 kHz. À l'écoute, ce comportement se traduit par des aigus trop incisifs et une sensation de brillance gênante. Les cymbales, notamment, sonnent agressivement, voire se montrent vite fatigantes sur certains enregistrements.
Le résultat est une signature sonore assez particulière : des voix correctement mises en avant, des graves largement en retrait et des aigus qui manquent de douceur. Heureusement, le niveau de détail est plutôt satisfaisant si l'on parvient à outrepasser ces forts déséquilibres.
Isolation acoustique : la ville s'invite dans la musique
Autre point faible, et non des moindres : l'isolation acoustique. Avec ses petites mousses simplement posées sur les oreilles, le MDR-3R ne constitue pratiquement aucune barrière contre les bruits environnants. Voitures, conversations et autres nuisances urbaines restent très perceptibles, même lorsque la musique joue. Il faut dire que la conception très ouverte de ce casque ne favorise absolument pas l'atténuation passive.
Là encore, nos mesures sont sans appel : l'atténuation demeure proche de 0 dB sur la quasi-totalité des fréquences. Autrement dit, le MDR-3R laisse passer l'essentiel des bruits extérieurs.
Cette faible isolation peut permettre de conserver une bonne perception de son environnement, mais elle nuit considérablement à l'immersion musicale dans les lieux bruyants. Et pousser le volume pour compenser n'est évidemment pas une solution recommandable.
Nos premières impressions : la nostalgie ne fait pas tout
Le Sony MDR-3R est un objet attachant. Son esthétique rétro, ses mousses orange et sa simplicité d'utilisation lui confèrent une personnalité que beaucoup de casques modernes pourraient lui envier.
Mais dès que l'on s'intéresse à ses performances, le tableau devient nettement moins séduisant. Entre un maintien et des sensations de confort perfectibles, une isolation acoustique inexistante, des basses anémiques et des aigus agressifs, difficile de le recommander à ceux qui placent la qualité sonore au premier rang de leurs priorités.
À environ 70 €, le MDR-3R apparaît donc davantage comme un accessoire rétro destiné aux amoureux du look Walkman que comme un casque capable de rivaliser avec les références audio actuelles.
Un bel hommage au passé, assurément. Mais aussi la preuve que, dans le domaine du son, tout n'était pas forcément mieux avant.

articles.title: Google se débarrasse de son mythique bouton de recherche en faveur de l’IA — Frandroid
articles.text:
Si vous aviez encore des doutes sur les priorités de Google, le dernier message de Robby Stein sur X devrait vous les ôter. Comme l’a repéré Android Authority, le vice-président produit de Google Search a détaillé, le 19 novembre, les nouveautés qui arrivent sur la célébrissime page d’accueil du moteur de recherche dans sa version pour ordinateur, ainsi que les fonctionnalités qui s’en vont.
Parmi ces dernières, on en compte une et pas des moindres : le bouton de recherche sur le web. Après de premiers tests menés en août dernier, l’entreprise retire bel et bien le bouton associé à la fonction qui a fait son succès.
Google met le turbo sur l’IA
Sur la page que l’on peut voir dans la courte vidéo de démo, la « Recherche Google » a été remplacée par trois autres boutons, tous liés à l’IA. Un premier qui propose de créer des images via Nano Banana, un second qui permet « d’interroger » un fichier à l’aide de l’IA et un troisième qui promet sobrement de vous aider à « brainstormer ». Étrangement, le bouton « J’ai de la chance » résiste encore et toujours à l’envahisseur, même s’il ne semble plus vraiment correspondre aux nouvelles priorités de l’entreprise.
Du 19 au 30 novembre, le Plaud Note Pro passe à 149 € au lieu de 189 € ! Il enregistre vos réunions, les transcrit et les synthétise pour vous, il suffit d’appuyer sur un bouton. Les Plaud Note, NotePin et NotePin S sont aussi à -20 %. Bref, c’est le moment d’arrêter de perdre du temps au travail !
Bien évidemment, il sera toujours possible de lancer une recherche Google avec une simple pression de la touche Entrée ou via la barre de recherche du navigateur, mais la page d’accueil du site ne met clairement plus la recherche en avant. Sous la barre, l’espace autrefois réservé à la recherche classique renvoie désormais vers les outils d’IA de Google.
Plus aucune raison de quitter Google
D’ailleurs, les autres changements apportés à la très minimaliste page d’accueil du site le prouvent. Un panneau latéral sur la gauche permet de lancer de nouveaux « fils » de discussion IA, de voir les tendances de recherche du moment et d’accéder à son historique de recherches en mode IA ainsi qu’à feu NotebookLM. Google calque ainsi un peu plus sa page d’accueil sur l’interface de Gemini, son chatbot, en mettant l’IA au cœur de l’expérience Google.
Ce panneau ne s’affiche que si vous êtes connecté à votre compte Google, et on le retrouve aussi sur la page de résultats.
« Les utilisateurs se tournent vers Search avec davantage de questions qui ne se résument pas à une recherche ponctuelle ; lors de nos tests, cette barre latérale a fait une vraie différence pour avancer et continuer à explorer le web », se vante d’ailleurs Robby Stein. Google préfère clairement vous garder dans son interface conversationnelle plutôt que de vous envoyer sur d’autres sites, même si le mode IA continue d’afficher des liens vers les pages qu’il utilise.
    Pour aller plus loin
Gemini Notebook : Google prépare un mode « coach » qui corrige vos idées sans écrire à votre place
            
Cette nouveauté est en cours de déploiement dans le monde entier, uniquement sur la page d’accueil pour ordinateur, et elle arrive progressivement : elle peut donc mettre quelques jours, voire quelques semaines, à s’afficher chez vous.
Les internautes français sont bien concernés : le mode IA de Google est disponible en France depuis le 22 juillet 2026, sur ordinateur, sur mobile et dans l’application Google.

articles.title: Florence Pugh, Kristen Stewart... Quelle James Bond girl pour accompagner Robert Pattinson ?
articles.text:
James Bond a un nouveau visage. À la surprise générale, Amazon MGM Studios a choisi Robert Pattinson pour le 26e film, réalisé par Denis Villeneuve et écrit par Steven Knight. Il succède à Daniel Craig, qui a incarné le célèbre espion britannique dans cinq films.
Le rôle-titre est donc attribué. Maintenant, on veut savoir qui donnera la réplique à Robert Pattinson. Il y a l’identité du futur méchant, très importante, et il y a aussi celle de la James Bond girl (il peut y en avoir plusieurs). Dans Mourir peut attendre, sorti en 2021, Léa Seydoux et Ana de Armas accompagnaient Daniel Craig.
Nos candidates favorites pour la prochaine James Bond girl
Inde Navarrette
Inde Navarrette est LA révélation de cette année 2026. Elle a profondément marqué les esprits grâce à son rôle dans le film d’horreur Obsession, où elle captive par ses grimaces impressionnantes et ses changements de ton flippants. Il faut s’attendre à la voir de plus en plus dans les grosses productions. Marvel l’a d’ailleurs choisie pour incarner Malicia dans son nouveau film X-Men, attendu en salles en mai 2028. Son nom circulait aussi pour Heat 2, la suite du film de Michael Mann. En devenant la future James Bond Girl, elle cimenterait toujours plus sa place à Hollywood.
Anya Taylor-Joy
Anya Taylor-Joy a déjà une carrière bien remplie. Elle a déjà un pied dans plusieurs grandes sagas, de Mad Max (Furiosa) à Dune. Elle sera aussi dans Le Seigneur des anneaux : La Chasse à Gollum, attendu en salles en décembre 2027. Son aura mystérieuse en ferait une James Bond girl de premier choix face à un Robert Pattinson au charme assez similaire. On a vraiment envie de voir cette alchimie à l’écran.
Vanessa Kirby
Vanessa Kirby a déjà prouvé qu’elle savait s’imposer dans les grosses productions d’action. Vue dans Mission : Impossible aux côtés de Tom Cruise et dans Fast and Furious : Hobbs & Shaw, elle maîtrise parfaitement les codes du film d’espionnage et le jeu physique. L’actrice britannique, que l’on a aussi retrouvée dans le costume de Sue Storm pour Les Quatre Fantastiques chez Marvel, possède exactement ce mélange de froideur aristocratique et d’autorité naturelle. Face au James Bond plus sombre et nerveux annoncé avec Robert Pattinson, elle ferait une alliée redoutable, ou une agente double particulièrement crédible.
Simone Ashley
Révélée au grand public grâce à la deuxième saison de Bridgerton, la comédienne britannique possède l’élégance et le charisme nécessaires pour reprendre le flambeau des grandes James Bond girls. Loin de se cantonner aux drames en costumes, Simone Ashley s’est tournée vers des productions plus musclées, notamment dans F1 aux côtés de Brad Pitt, prouvant qu’elle a tout à fait sa place dans un blockbuster à grand spectacle. Son profil apporterait un vrai vent de fraîcheur à la franchise, dans la lignée directe du passage éclair mais marquant d’Ana de Armas dans Mourir peut attendre.
Florence Pugh
Difficile de trouver une actrice plus solide à Hollywood actuellement. Qu’elle porte le drame (Les Filles du Docteur March, Oppenheimer), le thriller (Don’t Worry Darling) ou l’action pure avec son rôle de Yelena Belova dans l’univers Marvel (Black Widow, Thunderbolts), Florence Pugh imprime l’écran à chaque apparition. Avec son franc-parler, son énergie brute et son jeu très physique, elle est l’exact opposé d’une simple potiche de luxe. L’associer à Robert Pattinson devant la caméra de Denis Villeneuve, qui la connaît déjà très bien depuis Dune : Deuxième Partie, garantirait une dynamique électrique et moderne pour relancer 007.
Kristen Stewart
Imaginez les retrouvailles légendaires. Dix-huit ans après le premier Twilight (2008), Kristen Stewart et Robert Pattinson se retrouveraient dans un film James Bond. Une manière de boucler la boucle, même si cela relèverait plus du troll que de la proposition vraiment sérieuse. Notons quand même que Kristen Stewart n’est pas 100 % étrangère au genre espionnage, puisqu’elle a joué dans le film Charlie’s Angels.

articles.title: US-IT-Chaos: Wie du erkennst, ob es sich um Ausfälle oder Cyberangriffe handelt
articles.text:
Nur 1 von 1.000 Ausfällen ist ein Hack: Wie du erkennst, ob hinter einer IT-Störung wirklich ein Cyberangriff steckt
In den USA häufen sich seit Mitte November 2026 IT-Ausfälle, von denen Millionen Nutzer:innen weltweit betroffen sind. So fielen mehrere Cloud-Dienste von Microsoft aus, darunter Outlook und Teams. Auch bei der US-Luftfahrtbehörde FAA, dem US-Geheimdienst NSA oder Online-Diensten von Apple kam es zu Störungen.
USA sehen keine Belege für Cyberangriffe
Beobachter:innen spekulieren aufgrund der Häufung und vor dem Hintergrund von tatsächlichen Cyberangriffen auf Supermärkte, Dienstleister und Behörden in Europa über entsprechende Attacken von Hacker:innen. US-Außenminister Marco Rubio erklärte dagegen am 17. November 2026, dass es „keinerlei Belege oder Gründe für diese Annahme“ gebe, wie das ZDF berichtet.
Die Kolleg:innen von Wired haben einen Guide mit verschiedenen Fragen erstellt, die sich Nutzer:innen stellen können. Die Beantwortung soll dann dazu beitragen, besser einschätzen zu können, ob es sich um Ausfälle oder Cyberattacken handelt.
Suche nach technischen Fehlern
Zunächst einmal sollte die Suche nach technischen Fehlern Priorität haben. IT-Expert:innen gehen jedenfalls davon aus, dass fehlerhafte Softwareupdates, Änderungen an der Konfiguration oder beschädigte Kabel oder Geräte deutlich häufiger vorkommen als Cyberangriffe.
Doug Madory vom IT-Sicherheitsunternehmen Infoblox schätzt gegenüber Wired, dass bei den von ihm beobachteten Netzwerkausfällen nur einer von tausend auf einen Hackerangriff zurückging. Danach sollten Nutzer:innen die Statusseiten und offizielle Mitteilungen von Betreibern betroffener Dienste prüfen. Je mehr Firmen auf große Cloud-Anbieter wie AWS setzen, desto mehr Dienste und Kund:innen können von einem dort auftretenden Problem betroffen sein.
Mithilfe von Diensten wie Cloudflare Radar lässt sich zudem einfach ermitteln, ob nur ein Anbieter oder mehrere Netzwerke in der Region von Ausfällen betroffen sind. Daran kann man ablesen, ob es sich um ein fehlerhaftes Update bei einem Betreiber oder etwa um ein beschädigtes Glasfaserkabel handeln könnte.
Bekennerschreiben von Ransomware-Gruppen
Hinweise auf Cyberangriffe liefern dagegen mögliche Bekennerschreiben, etwa von Ransomware-Gruppen. Diese sind allerdings mit Vorsicht zu genießen, da solche Behauptungen übertrieben oder erfunden sein könnten, wie Wired warnt. Eine Bestätigung können Mitteilungen der betroffenen Organisation, von Behörden oder unabhängigen Sicherheitsforscher:innen liefern.
Einen weiteren Anhaltspunkt kann auch die Dauer des Ausfalls liefern. Geht es um ein fehlerhaftes Update, ist das oft innerhalb von Minuten oder Stunden geregelt. Bei einer Ransomware-Attacke kann es dagegen Tage, Wochen oder Monate dauern, bis ausgefallene Dienste wieder normal funktionieren.
Technik wird immer komplexer
Im Fall der aktuellen IT-Ausfälle in den USA kommt noch ein weiterer Punkt dazu, der eine genauere Betrachtung verdient: die zeitliche Nähe der Angriffe. Experte Madory erklärt allerdings, dass die Serie an Störungen auch schlicht zeigen könnte, wie komplex die Technik geworden sei.
„In unserer Gesellschaft läuft alles über internetbasierte Dienste. Und die fallen von Zeit zu Zeit aus“, so Madory gegenüber Wired. Solche Ausfälle ließen sich nie ganz verhindern. Wichtig sei zu verstehen, was jeden einzelnen Ausfall ausmache und was man daraus lernen könne.

articles.title: Alemania diseña, China pone la base y España fabrica: así se hará el próximo Opel eléctrico
articles.text:
Adaptarse o morir, incluso aunque la adaptación sea síntoma de la gravedad de un sector, el automotor, que hubo un tiempo que fue el motor de la industria alemana y europea. Opel y Leapmotor han sellado el acuerdo por el que la empresa china prestará sus servicios de ingeniería y desarrollo para el próximo SUV eléctrico de la mítica escuadra teutona.
100 millones para tener lo mejor de los dos mundos. Leapmotor comunicó el pasado 20 de noviembre a la Bolsa de Hong Kong este contrato por valor de 100 millones de euros. Según Florian Huettl, CEO de Opel, el acuerdo es un puente entre dos ecosistemas tecnológicos sólidos para tener ambos mundos. "Este enfoque vanguardista de desarrollo conjunto reúne velocidad, solidez tecnológica y experiencia en ingeniería para crear un nuevo y sumamente atractivo C-SUV de Opel para nuestros clientes".
Los equipos de ambas compañías ya trabajan en centros conjuntos en Hangzhou y Rüsselsheim. La división de tareas es clara: Leapmotor aporta sus componentes centrales, Opel pone su diseño, la ergonomía del habitáculo, la ingeniería del chasis, la iluminación y los asientos. La fabricación está prevista en la planta de Stellantis en Zaragoza. El proyecto comenzará ya en 2026 y se dilatará hasta 2028, ya que el inicio de producción está previsto para septiembre de ese año.
Por qué importa. Durante décadas, Europa recurría a China para una fabricación en cadena abaratando costes y también durante décadas, China recurría a la tecnología europea para sus bólidos. Pero se han cambiado las tornas y ahora una marca histórica alemana busca apoyo en una empresa china para para su futuro coche eléctrico. Y tiene tres buenas razones de peso: el tiempo, el precio y la fábrica. ¿A qué precio? Pues Stellantis ha recortado 650 puestos de ingeniería de Opel en Alemania, una señal de que el I+D se está desplazando hacia China.
El comunicado en Stellantis Media recoge que esta alianza le permite desarrollar el coche en menos de dos años a partir de una arquitectura eléctrica ya validada, mucho más rápido que empezar de cero y también mucho más barato. Por otro lado, es un espaldarazo más a la experiencia y saber hacer de Figueruelas: lleva fabricando el Opel Corsa desde 1982 y ya ha superado más de 10 millones de unidades y esta nueva línea refuerza su futuro.
El culebrón Stellantis - Leapmotor - Opel. Allá por octubre de 2023, Stellantis compró aproximadamente el 20% de Leapmotor y juntas crearon Leapmotor International, una empresa conjunta (51 % Stellantis, 49 % Leapmotor) con derechos exclusivos de venta y fabricación fuera de la Gran China. Como Stellantis es dueña de Opel y además es accionista de Leapmotor, este contrato de 100 millones cuenta como una operación entre empresas vinculadas, de ahí que Leapmotor tuviera que comunicarlo a la Bolsa de Hong Kong.
China se está comiendo el mercado. Las marcas chinas alcanzaron el 12,7 % de las matriculaciones europeas en el tercer trimestre de 2026, según Dataforce, una subida notable desde el 1% de cuota que tenían hace solo un lustro. Desde que la UE anunció los aranceles a los eléctricos fabricados en China, muchas marcas chinas se han adaptador trasladando parte de su producción a Europa u orientándose hacia los híbridos. En cualquier caso, el ecosistema de marcas, modelos, prestaciones y precios de China hace que resistirse sea una misión casi imposible, tanto para fabricantes como para clientes.
100 millones son solo el principio. Hay muchas incógnitas relativas a este nuevo coche eléctrico de Opel para 2028, como sus dimensiones definitivas, la batería y su autonomía, precio o cómo se enmarca dentro de la gama de la marca, si bien se rumorea que será un SUV de unos 4,50 metros situado entre Frontera y Grandland, y de arquitectura eléctrica y baterías LFP de Leapmotor.
Para Leapmotor, este proyecto se integra dentro del plan FaSTLane 2030 de Stellantis y espera suministrar componentes durante la vida del modelo y ojo porque esta aportación es independiente de este acuerdo. ¿Qué quiere decir esto? Que aparte tendrán que negociar, cerrar y pagar ese suministro.

articles.title: Por que cada lado do cérebro controla o lado oposto do corpo?
articles.text:
Neurocientistas da Universidade de Minnesota propuseram uma nova hipótese evolutiva para explicar por que o lado direito do cérebro controla o lado esquerdo do corpo e vice-versa.
Publicado na revista Frontiers in Neuroanatomy, o estudo de Martin Wessendorf e Daniel Wang sugere que essa organização cruzada começou no sistema visual de peixes sem mandíbula, há mais de 500 milhões de anos.
Origem na visão e adaptação evolutiva
Em vez de realizar novos experimentos ou descobrir fósseis, Wessendorf e Wang revisaram estudos anteriores sobre os principais grupos de vertebrados, dos anfíbios aos mamíferos. O objetivo foi comparar como as conexões nervosas cruzadas se desenvolveram e se sobrepuseram entre diferentes espécies.
Segundo os pesquisadores, o primeiro cruzamento provavelmente ocorreu na visão. Os olhos dos peixes sem mandíbula invertiam naturalmente a luz recebida, fazendo com que os sinais de cada olho fossem enviados ao lado oposto do cérebro, em direção a uma região chamada teto óptico. Nos mamíferos, a estrutura correspondente é o colículo superior.
Com o desenvolvimento de outros sistemas sensoriais, informações relacionadas ao tato, à vibração e à dor também teriam seguido esse padrão.
“Propomos que a organização contralateral do teto óptico tenha influenciado a evolução subsequente dos sistemas sensoriais e motores em direção a uma organização contralateral”, escreveram os pesquisadores.
Quando os mamíferos verdadeiros surgiram, há aproximadamente 165 milhões de anos, os sistemas somatossensorial, rubroespinal e tectoespinal já existiam com organização cruzada havia quase 200 milhões de anos.
Explicações anteriores e próximos testes
Para Wessendorf e Wang, a evolução do córtex cerebral dos mamíferos aproveitou as conexões que já estavam estabelecidas. Seria mais econômico desenvolver novas estruturas sobre esse padrão do que reorganizar todo o sistema nervoso.
A interpretação também questiona explicações anteriores, como a possibilidade de o cruzamento ser resultado de uma vantagem de eficiência ou de uma torção no corpo de um ancestral comum dos vertebrados. Na avaliação dos autores, essas hipóteses não contemplam toda a trajetória evolutiva das conexões cerebrais.
A teoria ainda precisa ser confrontada com novas evidências. Os pesquisadores apontam três caminhos para aprofundar a investigação:
- Registros fósseis: procurar evidências adicionais em fósseis, especialmente de peixes sem mandíbula com cerca de 500 milhões de anos.
- Mapeamento neural: analisar as conexões cerebrais de crocodilos e aves, grupos ainda não completamente estudados nesse aspecto.
- Eficiência das conexões: verificar a previsão de que a organização cruzada é mais eficiente do que alternativas em que cada hemisfério controla o mesmo lado do corpo.
A proposta também procura preencher uma lacuna na literatura científica: embora existam estudos sobre lateralização cerebral publicados ao longo de aproximadamente 50 anos, os autores observam que faltava uma síntese dessas pesquisas sob uma perspectiva evolutiva.
Valdir Antonelli é jornalista com especialização em marketing digital e consumo.

articles.title: Intel secures first external customer for 18A-P node, CEO Lip-Bu Tan says
articles.text:
The big picture: In a key development that could give a much-needed boost to its turnaround plans, beleaguered chipmaker Intel has reportedly secured its first external customer for its advanced 18A-P chip manufacturing process. The announcement was made by Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan at the TomorrowX Summit in Austin last week, although he did not publicly identify the customer.
The news was reiterated by Intel's chief technology officer, Pushkar Ranade, who clarified that Tan was talking about the cutting-edge 18A-P node rather than the base 18A. Though both are 1.8nm-class process nodes, Intel claims that the newer technology delivers around 9% higher performance at the same power or consumes 18% lower power while delivering the same performance.
 – Pushkar Ranade (@magicsilicon) November 18, 2026
Other notable changes implemented in 18A-P include the addition of Power Boost dual-contact, low-resistance transistors for higher drive current and frequency, a fifth logic Vt pair between ULVT and LVT for designers to balance speed and power, and mobility enhancement through PMOS via strain engineering for greater efficiency.
At the same event, Tan also revealed that Intel's 18A yields have reached 70%, up significantly from last year. He did not specify whether he was referring to functional die yield or parametric yield, though industry convention suggests it's the former, which describes the percentage of dies that pass basic electrical and functional testing.
The 18A process is currently used in Intel's Core Ultra 300-series Panther Lake client CPUs and Xeon 6+ Clearwater Forest data center processors. The chipmaker claims that 18A delivers up to 18% higher performance at the same power, 38% lower power at the same performance, and 1.3 times the chip density compared to Intel 3.
Meanwhile, Microsoft has announced that it will adopt Intel's EMIB advanced packaging technology for its in-house Azure processors, making it the first company to publicly confirm using Intel's 2.5D packaging solution for its in-house silicon. The company added that it has also signed a multi-year deal with the chipmaker to buy Xeon processors, including the upcoming Diamond Rapids chips.
The improving 18A yields and the deals with Microsoft and the unnamed foundry client could be the beginning of a potential turnaround for Intel, which has suffered one blow after another in recent years. However, despite the string of positive news, the company's stock fell nearly 8% on Friday, closing at $51.28, down nearly two-thirds from its June 2026 peak of $140.94.

articles.title: Nintendo’s Switch 2 console is $50 off for Black Friday
articles.text:
Those hoping to save some cash on a Nintendo Switch 2 can do so starting today, November 22nd, through Saturday, December 5th, giving you plenty of time to think about it after Cyber Monday has passed. For a limited time, Nintendo has knocked $50 off one of its two current console bundles, temporarily rolling back the $50 price increase that went into effect in early September.
Nintendo’s Switch 2 console is $50 off for Black Friday
The hybrid handheld / home console was already one of the best values in gaming, and now it’s an even better deal.
It’s tough to predict which bundle will be most popular for your household. The Mario Kart World bundle runs $499.99 (previously $549.99) and includes the console, a digital copy of the aforementioned game, and three months of Nintendo Switch Online. Then there’s the Nintendo Switch Sports Resort bundle for $529.99 (price unchanged for Black Friday), which includes the more recent minigame-filled title instead. Both are currently available from Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart, and Nintendo.
Nintendo has delivered hit after hit since the console launched in mid-2025. There are now plenty of excellent games to justify snagging a Switch 2, including, most recently, the stellar remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Plus, the newer console can play nearly all of the original Switch games, and it’s wirelessly compatible with the older system’s Joy-Con and Switch Pro controllers.
If you’re planning to get a Switch 2, below are some useful guides filled with accessory recommendations. From tempered glass screen protectors and protective cases to controllers, there are plenty of goodies that’ll help you take better care of your Switch 2 and get more enjoyment from it.

articles.title: CISA flags critical Cisco RCE flaw as actively exploited in attacks
articles.text:
The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) warned federal agencies that attackers are now exploiting a recently patched critical Cisco Expressway vulnerability in the wild.
Cisco Expressway Series devices are enterprise collaboration gateways (deployed as virtual machines or physical hardware appliances) that connect internal voice and video systems with outside networks and remote users via a secure connection.
Tracked as CVE-2026-76466, this security flaw stems from the use of hard-coded credentials and a failure to fully validate client certificates, enabling unauthenticated attackers to remotely execute arbitrary operating system commands as root on affected Cisco Expressway-C and Cisco Expressway-E devices configured in a cluster.
"An attacker with possession of the cookies could exploit this vulnerability by connecting to the database service and invoking specific remote procedure call (RPC) commands," Cisco said in late October, when it released security patches to address the issue.
While Cisco says that its Product Security Incident Response Team (PSIRT) is not aware of active exploitation in the wild or publicly available proof-of-concept exploits targeting this vulnerability, CISA tagged it as actively exploited on Friday.
The cybersecurity agency also added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog on Tuesday and ordered US Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies to secure their systems within three days, as mandated by Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04.
Although BOD 26-04 targets only federal agencies, CISA urged all network defenders, including private-sector security teams, to prioritize patching this flaw to block ongoing attacks that may target their networks.
"These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise," it warned.
Exploited to gain root on Internet-exposed devices
While CISA has yet to share details on these ongoing attacks, Russian cybersecurity company F6 said on Thursday that it spotted attackers using an unnamed AI assistant to successfully exploit CVE-2026-7646 and gain remote command execution with full root privileges on Internet-exposed Cisco Expressway devices.
"The attackers initially compromised two Cisco Expressway internet-facing devices. Through one of them, they gained access to two additional cluster nodes located on the organization’s internal network," F6 security researchers noted.
"After obtaining root access, the attackers began preparing tooling for further lateral movement across the infrastructure. They used custom Python scripts designed to scan the network, discover accessible SMB resources, interact with SQL Server and WinRM, and explore GitLab repositories in order to exfiltrate credentials and other sensitive information."
Two weeks ago, CISA also flagged a high-severity Cisco BroadWorks vulnerability (CVE-2026-20320) as actively exploited in attacks and ordered federal agencies to patch their systems by November 24.
According to threat intelligence firm Malbear Labs, a Chinese-speaking threat actor abused CVE-2026-20320 in autonomous AI attacks targeting a European telecommunications provider and 13 organizations that used its data centers and cloud infrastructure.
CISA has added 103 Cisco vulnerabilities to its list of actively exploited flaws since November 2021, seven of which ransomware gangs have also used in the wild.

articles.title: Hackers exploit GL.iNet cloud flaw to infect routers, KVM devices
articles.text:
GL.iNet has confirmed that hackers exploited a vulnerability in its cloud remote management services to install custom malware on customers' routers and KVM devices, with some affected users reporting backdoors and reverse shells giving remote access to infected devices.
GL.iNet manufactures networking equipment, including home and travel routers, as well as KVM devices that allow users to access and control computers remotely.
Its GoodCloud platform allows customers to remotely manage supported devices, including accessing and controlling computers and servers connected to its KVM products.
In a security advisory published on November 20, GL.iNet confirmed that an unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in its cloud remote management services to access devices and install malicious software.
"The attack path has been blocked. We fixed the cloud vulnerability and blocked the access used in this incident," the company said.
"Devices can no longer be newly infected through this attack path. These measures do not remove malware from devices that were already infected."
GL.iNet has not disclosed how the attackers exploited its cloud platform, how many customers were impacted, or whether information was stolen from compromised devices.
The company is also investigating whether computers connected to infected KVM devices were compromised.
GL.iNet recommends that customers check their devices for signs of infection and install the latest security firmware, even if no malware is detected.
The company's initial instructions told customers to look for a process running as crond -i /tmp/.log, which GL.iNet said was an indicator of compromise.
While the cloud vulnerability has been fixed, GL.iNet says stable firmware updates containing additional security fixes for both routers and KVM devices are scheduled for release on November 22, 2026.
For KVM devices, customers can follow the company's firmware upgrade guidance, which recommends version 1.10.3 or later for the RM10, RM1, RM1V2, RM1PE, and RM4PE, version 1.10.3 beta or later for the RM10RC, and version 1.8.7 or later for the RMQ1.
Router owners should install the latest security firmware for their specific model as soon as it becomes available.
However, GL.iNet forum members warn that the company's detection instructions may not identify all compromised devices, including those infected with other backdoors or running reverse shells.
GL.iNet has linked to a community-developed detection and cleanup tool as part of the company's official support instructions for routers and KVM devices.
The scanner performs additional checks for known malware files, suspicious processes, modified system utilities, and configuration files modified for persistence. It can also collect forensic evidence and optionally remove known malware components.
The project's developers warn that the scanner cannot detect every infection and that compromised devices may require reinstalling firmware without retaining existing settings, as malicious files stored in configuration directories could survive an ordinary firmware upgrade.
Customers who suspect their devices were compromised should preserve evidence before resetting them, avoid restoring potentially infected configurations, and rotate credentials and access keys that may have been exposed.
GL.iNet also asked customers who run the scanner to upload the anonymous report when prompted so the developers can determine the number and types of devices impacted.
For KVM users, the malware may have allowed access to the computers controlled by the KVM, so those devices should also be analyzed for potential compromise.
Malware and reverse shells discovered
Following the disclosure, GL.iNet customers and security researchers shared evidence of custom malware infections designed specifically for GL.iNET devices, as well as root-level reverse shells that connected compromised routers to the IP address 170.39.226[.]219.
The reverse shells used the Linux nc utility to create outbound connections, allowing remote attackers to execute commands on infected devices.
Researchers at RemoteToHome Consulting also identified a potential command injection vulnerability in GL.iNet's GoodCloud client involving a handler used for AstroWarp/SD-WAN functionality.
According to the researchers, the handler passes cloud-supplied values into shell commands executed with root privileges without properly validating them.
However, GL.iNet has not confirmed that this particular vulnerability was used in the attacks.
RemoteToHome says it analyzed 183 routers it owns or manages and found suspicious activity on 152, including 24 with root-level reverse shells, 47 with an older persistent backdoor, and 81 showing evidence that attacker-supplied commands had executed.
The researchers note that their findings may not be the same as the other GL.iNet customers and that the older backdoor infections may not be linked to the November attacks.
In a separate forum report, the owner of a compromised GL-RM1 KVM shared network logs showing it downloading a malicious ni.sh script and additional executable payloads from 66.245.219[.]252 on November 19.
The owner also reported that the device began communicating with approximately 1,800 residential IP addresses daily and repeatedly contacted the TRON blockchain API, exhibiting activity suggestive of a peer-to-peer network.
However, the purpose of these connections is unclear, and there is no confirmation that the compromised devices were being used as residential proxies or were part of a larger botnet.
BleepingComputer examined a copy of the malicious ni.sh script [VirusTotal] and found that it contains code specifically tailored to GL.iNet routers and KVM devices.
The script recognizes numerous GL.iNet device models and downloads malicious executables named gl-helper and gb from hardcoded servers.
It also establishes persistence through startup scripts and scheduled tasks, allowing the malware to restart after a reboot or if its processes are terminated.
The installer includes functionality to disguise the malicious process as crond -i /tmp/.log, matching the IOC published by GL.iNet.
An interesting feature is replacing the legitimate netstat utility with a modified shell script that filters out connections to 66.245.219[.]252, potentially hiding the malware's communications from administrators examining network connections.
The installer also contains functionality to install SSH public keys for remote access, modify file timestamps, and periodically contact a remote server to retrieve and execute commands.
The attacker's infrastructure includes two IP addresses, 66.245.219[.]252 and 65.20.71[.]131, which match the IP addresses seen in the compromised KVM owner's logs.
The script also contains Chinese-language developer comments describing its persistence mechanisms, reporting functionality, and interactions with GL.iNet's cloud management software, indicating a Chinese-speaking individual may have written it.
BleepingComputer also examined a separate malicious Lua payload recovered from a GL-MT2500 router.
The payload was launched through a modified urandom_seed startup script and included functionality to collect device information, contact remote servers, and download and execute additional programs.
Some of the malicious files recovered from GL.iNet devices had timestamps dating to December 2025, suggesting that some devices may have been compromised for months. However, it is unclear whether these infections involved the same threat actors or were related to the November 20 attacks.
GL.iNet says it continues to investigate the incident and plans to notify identified affected customers using the email addresses associated with their cloud accounts.
